articleTitle: Job Mapping of Graduates of the UPI Fashion Design Education Study Program: Linearity Analysis and Career Determining Factors
abstract: This research aims to describe (1) the latest data on graduates of the UPI Fashion Design Education Study Program, consisting of the number of graduates, the number of graduates who are working, the number of graduates who are not working, and the number of graduates who are continuing their studies; (2) comparison of the number of graduates of the UPI Fashion Design Education Study Program who work according to the line of study program with those who do not suit their skills; (3) comparison of the number of graduates who are working, the number of graduates who are not working, and the number of graduates who are continuing their studies; 4) factors that influence graduate career choices. This research was conducted using survey techniques and processed using statistical calculations. The population that was also used as a sample in this research were all graduates of the UPI Fashion Design Education Study Program with the last 3 years (graduates in 2021, 2022 and 2023) as the sample. Data collection was carried out by distributing questionnaires to all predetermined samples. The collected data was analyzed using quantitative descriptive techniques and processed using the software for data calculation. The research results showed that there were 140 graduates in the period 2021–2023, with details of 45 people (graduates of 2021), 39 people (class of 2022), and 56 people (2023 graduate). The difference in the number of career choices for Fashion Design Education graduates recorded in 2024, there are 111 people (79%) who are working, 22 people (16%) are not / are not working, and 8 people (5%) are continuing their studies. The career distribution of graduates who work includes 89 people (80.1 % ) working linearly with a skills program, and 22 other people (19.9%) not linearly working with a skills program. The ratio between the number of graduates who work linearly with expertise and those who work non-linearly with expertise is 4:1, where the dominant career taken by graduates of the UPI Fashion Design Education Study Program is Clothing Industry Workers (Fashion Designer, Pattern Maker, Fashion Marchandising, etc.), Entrepreneur in the Field of Finance, and as a Teacher. The results of the research can help study programs to determine strategies in lectures or assist in the career aspiration guidance process for fashion design graduates in the career selection process.

articleTitle: The Design and Construction of an IoT Learning Board Using ESP32 and FPGA
abstract: This project develops an innovative educational board for learning about the Internet of Things (IoT), with a strong focus on enhancing STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) education. It combines an ESP32 chip for connectivity with a field-programmable gate array (FPGA) for flexible hardware design, creating a powerful tool for hands-on learning. The team refined the board through several prototypes to optimize it to meet the requirements and possible price. This unique combination allows students to explore real-world applications of STEM principles, particularly in hardware/software codesign and IoT technologies. Plans include expanding IoT features and investigating edge computing, further broadening its STEM applications. The primary goal is to provide educators and students with a practical platform to engage with advanced computer science, electrical engineering, and IoT concepts. By offering hands-on experience with cutting-edge technology, this project aims to inspire the next generation of STEM professionals and prepare them for careers in the rapidly evolving tech industry. This innovative approach to STEM education can help bridge the gap between theoretical knowledge and practical skills in IoT and related fields.

articleTitle: Transforming Children's Python Turtle Graphics Learning with LLM Technology: A Design Proposal
abstract: STEM education, particularly programming and coding, is of great importance in today's technological landscape. Turtle graphics, an effective tool for teaching programming concepts to children, is widely used in languages such as Python, known for its simplicity and readability. However, coding can be challenging for young learners, necessitating individualized support from teachers. Large language models (LLMs), which are already employed in debugging, present an opportunity to enhance educational support systems by providing personalized hints without revealing answers, thus preserving the educational value. This proposal aims to explore the use of LLMs to generate tailored hints and explanations for different age groups and skill levels, creating a dynamic and responsive learning environment. Additionally, the proposed system includes task creation that adapts to the student's previous performance and completed tasks, ensuring continuous and appropriately challenging learning experiences. The goal of our research is to design a support system that leverages LLM technology to improve children and young students' learning in Python Turtle graphics. This system promises personalized educational support and adaptive task generation, enhancing the overall learning experience for young programmers. Future studies are necessary to test this system with real users, evaluate its effectiveness, and refine its design based on practical feedback.

articleTitle: Introducing Secondary School Students to Telecommunications Engineering Through the WiFinder Project: Part I – Implementation of Handheld Device
abstract: Engineering workshop plays an essential role in the development of practical skills and knowledge. It serves as an experiential learning environment where theoretical concepts are transformed into real-world solutions through hands-on activities. The availability of proper tools is crucial in ensuring the effectiveness of the workshop. Creating an in-house radio source locator for the training program offers several significant advantages, such as a cost-effective solution, and customization of features to support intended lessons. This paper describes the design and implementation of an in-house radio direction finder utilizing WiFi technology in the 2.4 GHz band. The device employed an ESP32 embedded board with a touchscreen for the user interface and measurement display. The resulting finder was able to show the signal strength of the selected WiFi access point and its direction. The screen interface allowed users to scan and select the WiFi source in the receiving range. The radio direction finding device was powered by a Lithium-ion battery which was able to operate continuously for at least 1 hour. The firmware update was designed to support the over-the-air approach. The deliverables for the training workshop consisted of a radio direction-finding unit, an omnidirectional antenna, a directional antenna, a charger, a handle, and mounting kits. A user manual and related instructional videos were available online for all trainees. This in-house device met the designed features and served its original purposes, especially customization and costeffectiveness.

articleTitle: The Effects of Kahoot! on Students’ Achievement in Math Classrooms
abstract: This study was conducted to investigate the impact of Kahoot! quizzes on students’ achievement. Kahoot! is a tool for using technology to administer quizzes, discussions or surveys. It is a game-based classroom response system played by the whole class in real time. Multiple-choice questions were projected on the screen. Students answered the questions with their smartphone, tablet or computer without creating their accounts. Weekly quizzes were used to test the effectiveness of the treatment regarding the students’ learning achievement. The participants in this study were 26 students enrolled in Pre-Calculus Section 1 using Kahoot!. 22 students enrolled in Section 2 using Kahoot!, and 17 students enrolled in the same course without Kahoot!. All three sections were taught by the same instructor at the University of Cincinnati Blue Ash College. Statistically significant results were observed for improvement in students’ achievement. The present analyses suggest that the students performed better at weekly assessments in classes that utilized Kahoot!

articleTitle: Collaborative Learning in Bilateral Academic Training on Robotics Design and Development
abstract: This paper presents how collaborative learning can facilitate academic training in robotics design and development, with the objective of establishing a foundation in robotics structure design and microcontroller programming for controlling robots, particularly for bilateral undergraduate students. The students comprise 20 engineering students and 20 architecture students, who are divided into groups of two, consisting of an engineering students and an architecture students each. Group activities focusing on robot structure design and robot Development are provided for the students. The results demonstrate that collaborative learning can effectively facilitate the training activities.

articleTitle: Semiconductor Synergy Capacity Building: Enhancing Laboratory Hands-On Excellence through University-Industry Collaboration
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive exploration of semiconductor synergy capacity building, emphasizing hands-on undergraduate engineering education to advance knowledge through university-industry collaboration. By leveraging practical experimentation and laboratory-based learning, students are equipped with the essential skills required for careers in the semiconductor industry. The paper elucidates laboratory procedures for testing critical parameters, with a focus on input offset voltage and output voltage swing testing of operational amplifiers (op-amps). A step-by-step guide is provided, enabling instructors and students to conduct these tests effectively. Additionally, the paper underscores the educational objectives of integrating parameter testing of op-amps into university laboratories, including the enhancement of practical skills, promotion of hands-on learning experiences, and alignment with industry demands. Through this collaborative approach, students are better prepared to address the challenges and opportunities within the semiconductor sector, ensuring a seamless transition from academia to industry.

articleTitle: Humans and AI: SWOT Analysis of Teaching Methods and Knowledge Acquisition of Students
abstract: In recent years, Artificial Intelligence (AI) has always been the top keyword in many fields, especially the field of education. In recent years, the education industry has always used artificial intelligence software as a tool to support learners in the field of teaching. But now, in many international articles, artificial intelligence has made many outstanding developments and has boldly raised the opinion that artificial intelligence can completely replace humans in the field of education. We conducted a survey with over 110 participants. The objective of this research article is to identify the strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and concepts (SWOT model) in the use of artificial intelligence in teaching methods and subsequent knowledge acquisition of pupil. The research article also gives examples of artificial intelligence in education.

articleTitle: Utilization of Remote Laboratory as STEM Implementation (Case Study of Mechatronics Competency)
abstract: The function of STEM can help with the learning process, including practicums, one of which is used in the remote laboratory. Practicum is a vital part of the learning process, particularly in the sciences and technology. A successful practicum demands a balance of equipment between the number of tools and participants, but in practice, the number of participants frequently considerably outnumbers the number of tools. One approach is to provide a remote laboratory that can be accessible from anywhere as long as it is connected to the internet and has a flexible schedule. The remote laboratory is made up of four major components: a server (which includes a computer or laptop), a processor, an actuator, and a camera. The second component is the internet device, the third is the user, and the fourth component is the software, which in this case includes ThinVNC, ngrok, and the given GUI. The remote laboratory requires assistance from all STEM elements in terms of compiling materials with a science approach, utilizing modern technology tools and requiring engineering to integrate them, as well as the role of mathematics in terms of using experimental data for statistical analysis. According to the findings of the STEM-based remote laboratory experiment, it provides the following benefits: It can bridge the gap between the number of tools and the number of users, give ease of scheduling, user access, and delivering materials, assignments.

articleTitle: Cultivating Design Thinking Competency Towards High School Students by using Real-World Problems
abstract: A specific design practice namely design thinking involves a problem-solving approach to deal with complex problems. Students had meaningful experiences in empathy, creativity, critical thinking, teamwork, and risk-taking, which prepared them for the next step of their learning or a career in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$21^{\text{st}}$</tex> century. A real-world problem is one of strategies for employing the obtained knowledge and particular skills to solve the problem. The study aims at cultivating five design thinking competencies of high school students by using real-world problem. The program was then designed to have fun, age-appropriate, practical, hand-on activities, and teamwork. After participation in the program designed, the high school students improved their design thinking competency and achieved the expected level of proficiency. Real-world problem motivated students' autonomy to find the right topic, create ideas, select the promising solution, construct a prototype, and test with the user. The students played an active role in gaining direct experiences. Moreover, a more favorable climate for learning by facilitators, teamwork, and program activity encouraged active participation of the students.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Impact of STEM Activities Related to the Ocean on Students' Gaining Ocean Literacy Based on Gender
abstract: This study investigates the effect of ocean-STEM activity on ocean literacy among 7th-grade students. The research design was a quasi-experimental non-equivalent pretest-posttest control group design. The research sample was determined randomly and divided into two groups: the experimental group (N=29), who carried out four ocean STEM activities, and the control group (N=31), who learned using traditional methods. Data collection used the Ocean Pollution Knowledge Test (OPKT) and the Ocean Attitude Survey (OAS). Students from the experimental group outperformed the control group significantly in both instruments, meaning that students involved in the ocean STEM activity significantly affected students’ ocean literacy. The study has implications for science teachers to use ocean-STEM activity to promote ocean literacy for junior high school students.

articleTitle: Effectiveness of Board Game Raising Stroke Awareness Among Young Children
abstract: Pre-hospital delays in stroke treatment in Thailand persist are due to a lack of public awareness regarding stroke symptoms and appropriate emergency responses. This study aims to develop and assess the effectiveness of an age-appropriate stroke board game to raise stroke awareness among young children in Thailand. The participants were comprised of 36 elementary school students from Naluang School, selected using a purposeful sampling technique. Data analysis involved a paired simple t-test. The results demonstrated that the board game effectively enhances stroke awareness among kids in grades 4-6 by engaging them in interactive play and an educational experience. The implication of this study suggests that the stroke board game approach could be employed in school settings to teach children about health-related topics.

articleTitle: The Role of Soft Skills in Developing Students’ Stem Competence
abstract: The purpose of this study is to determine the role of soft skills in developing STEM (science, technology, engineering and mathematics) competencies for students. The study will examine the benefits of developing soft skills for STEM students, and identify effective ways to practice these skills in students. The research will adopt qualitative methods of description, analysis and evaluation of documents or articles published domestically and internationally. The article will emphasize the role of soft skills including communication skills, problem solving skills, and teamwork skills. These 21st century skills are essential for students' future development. The results of the study also show that soft skills are currently very important and necessary for the development of students' STEM capabilities. This research article hopes to evaluate and show everyone the potential of soft skills in the 21st century, in addition to providing a more comprehensive and general perspective for educators to invest and develop. Improve soft skills in STEM learning of students in the 21st century.

articleTitle: Space STEM Education Guide for Global Positioning System Total Electron Content (GPS TEC)
abstract: This research focuses on designing a Space Science teaching model using a Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) education approach, specifically applying satellite technology in the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS), with an emphasis on Global Positioning System (GPS) satellites. The goal is to propose a new model in STEM education in Space Science by teaching GPS Total Electron Content (GPS TEC) variations in the ionosphere layer resulting from environmental changes on Earth, known as Lithosphere-Atmosphere-Ionosphere Coupling (LAIC). The teaching model was designed, named SPACE (S: Studying the problem, P: Planning and carrying out investigations, A: Analyzing and interpreting data, C: Critical thinking, Creative thinking, Collaborating, Communicating, and E: Evaluating, and Summarizing), serves as a guide for instructional management steps. The model was evaluated by five experts with at least 10 years of experience in Space Science. The evaluation of the appropriateness of the model for use as a teaching guideline resulted in the highest level of suitability <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\bar{x}= \mathbf{4.87},\ \mathbf{SD} =\mathbf{0.40})$</tex>.

articleTitle: Development of Learning Innovations Supporting Digital Electronics Technology Competency
abstract: Developing learning innovations supporting digital electronic technology competency is a goal to promote intelligent electronic performance. Technologists should have hands-on skills, troubleshooting, teamwork, and innovation skills. This research aims to develop learning innovations in digital electronic technology for teaching and learning at both vocational and higher education levels. The developed learning innovations include a digital technology practice package, teacher's manual, lesson plan, worksheet, presentation media, and test. The research tools were assessed for quality using 10 experts. The results of the student competency assessment included knowledge, skills, and personal characteristics. The research results found that the overall quality of the digital electronic technology-based learning innovations was at a high appropriate level (mean=4.28, S.D.=0.11). Learners were satisfied on average at a high level (mean = 4.42, S.D.=0.82). Learners had increased their expected competency after learning using developed learning innovations. However, good teaching management must consider various factors such as differences between students, how to learn linking theoretical content, and practical skills. The key goal is to provide learning that is consistent with the core competencies required by the industry.

articleTitle: The Alternative Peculiarity Divination System Fixed on FONDB-Mean Filter For Persistent Amplitude Impulsive Outlier
abstract: In peculiarity divination research society, the delineation units are hypothetically estimated as peculiarity delineation units or non-peculiarity delineation units. The theoretical analysis nominates the alternative peculiarity divination system fixed on the FONDB-Mean Filter (First Order Neighborhood Decision Based Mean Filter), that is elaborated for the original MDBUTMF (Modified decision based unsymmetric trimmed median filter) for revamping the accomplishment of the peculiarity divination system for PAIO (Persistent Amplitude Impulsive Outlier) at general peculiarity quantity (5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>-90<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>). In the analysis implementation, a lot of peculiarity delineations that are made up Lena, F16, Baboon and Pepper at general peculiarity quantity are used to investigate the accomplishment of the proposed peculiarity divination system, which is compared with many state-of-art systems: SMF, MF, AMF and MDBUTMF. articleTitle: Learning Management of Task-Based Learning Approach Together With Total Physical Response to Enhance the Speaking Skills of Primary 6 Students
abstract: This experimental research aimed to achieve two objectives: firstly, to assess the impact of the Task-Based Learning (TBL) approach together with Total Physical Response (TPR) on the speaking skills of Primary 6 students before and after instruction; secondly, to compare the speaking skills of students using the TBL-TPR approach with those using the Traditional method. The study involved sixty Primary 6 students from a school in Nonthaburi Province, Thailand, who were divided into experimental (n=30) and control (n=30) groups using cluster random sampling. The research instruments included a TBL-TPR learning management plan, Traditional lesson plans, and an English-speaking test. Data analysis was performed using statistical analysis software. Results revealed a significant improvement in the speaking skills of Primary 6 students after implementing the TBL-TPR approach, with post-intervention scores significantly higher than pre-intervention at a .05 level. Furthermore, students using the TBL-TPR approach demonstrated significantly higher speaking skills compared to those using the Traditional method at a .05 level. These findings highlight the effectiveness of integrating TBL with TPR in enhancing the speaking proficiency of Primary 6 students and underscore the importance of adopting innovative pedagogical approaches in language education to optimize learning outcomes.

articleTitle: Analysis of Research into the Teaching and Learning of Programming: An Updated Review
abstract: Around a decade ago, Salleh, Shukur, and Judi conducted a systematic review to analyse research on programming teaching tools. They identified a range of interesting findings from 45 scholarly articles that were published between 2005 and 2011. In our work, we reproduce this systematic study exactly, with the only deliberate change being that we consider works published from 2011 to 2022. Following the original methodology, a set of 26 research papers was selected. In the current work, the same research questions as the earlier study were considered, investigating (1) the issues discussed, (2) the methods used, (3) the types of tools involved, and (4) the level of programming expertise addressed. While one systematic review offers an overview of a field at a certain moment in time, two reviews carried out along the same lines but at distinct points in time allow for the identification of evolving patterns. Concretely, it was found that the more recent literature has a stronger emphasis on formal models and theories, greater reliance on surveys and empirical evaluations, and an increased interest in online tools.

articleTitle: Navigating the Era of Disruption in the Construction Industry in Indonesia: Challenges for TVET in Architecture
abstract: The growth of technology and the emergence of a challenging era of disruption have changed the paradigm of the construction industry in Indonesia. As an education that covers this, TVET needs to respond and prepare for this condition. Through industry surveys and literature studies, this research aims to describe the direction of development of the construction industry in the era of disruption. It was found that the adoption of technologies such as Building Information Modeling (BIM) is key to construction efficiency. However, challenges arise in integrating the required skills with the TVET curriculum.

articleTitle: Multi-sector Collaboration for Students of different levels to Learn Digital Technology Skills using Competency Assessment from Learning to Create pieces with a 3D printers for Young Innovators Case Study: MogroWittayakom School
abstract: This article is the result of collaboration across various associations to create learning spaces for students in compulsory and optional education as well as living skills. This article provides an example of learning digital technology skills through collaboration, starting with the establishment of an innovation room, followed by instructional activities to explore assessment methods for competency in creating works using a 3D printer tailored for young innovators. By employing rubric- based technology tailored to real-world conditions, it aims to fulfill teachers' expectations for student outcomes. This approach helps students understand and apply a rubric to evaluate and improve their own creations. The demographic involves 20 high school students from MogroWittayakhom, selected through purposive sampling. The students participated in a practical performance test, receiving step-by-step training over two days, totaling 12 hours. Upon completing the instruction, students designed and fabricated their projects using Tinkercad software, which were then printed with a 3D printer. The instructor evaluated the students using a rubric-based competency assessment with three scoring levels. The results showed that all 20 participants achieved a high competency level as per the rubric, validating the hypothesis with 100% of the participants meeting the performance criteria.

articleTitle: Development of a Training Course to Promote Non-Cognitive Skills Using Problem-Solving Learning for Automation Control
abstract: The research on this was to 1) develop a training course to promote non-cognitive skills, 2) find the index of the effectiveness of learning achievement training course 3) assess the skills that learners demonstrate during learning, and 4) to study the students' satisfaction toward with that learned the training course to promote non-cognitive skills using problem- solving learning for automation control. The samples were 150 students. The research results are shown as follows: 1) the development of a training course, the assessing the suitability of the training curriculum by the experts was found the developed curriculum was highly suitable, 2) learners who followed the designed learning model has higher learning achievement as 70% in average 3) the programming skills and non-cognitive skills of learners demonstrated the good level, 4) the students opinion for training course overall was at high level.

articleTitle: Project-Based Learning Integrating 5E Model for Improving Learning Outcome of Heat Transfer for Students in Mechanical Engineering Program
abstract: This paper introduces the implementation of a project-based learning (PjBL) method integrated with the 5E learning model during the introductory phase of PjBL. It aims to illustrate student learning outcomes and increased participation in the heat transfer subject of the Mechanical Engineering program. The chapter on convective heat transfer is selected for the PjBL strategy, involving grouping students and assigning a project to construct a roughness surface to increase the heat transfer rate in a solar air heater. The results show that all student groups were able to develop a project within the given timeframe, and learning achievements are on the rise. Additionally, the opinions of participants prove to be effective

articleTitle: Development of Innovation-based Learning on Basic Electronic Components
abstract: This paper presents the development of innovation-based learning on basic electronic components that is a key im-portant to making an innovation in the digital world and lifestyle. An idea of this research is to let the computer engineering students understanding how to control hardware with the basic electronic components by the hard-skills improvement, which is the basic concept for young innovator. The objective of this work is to propose in the main part of basic electronics components supported the real digital world using the innovation-based learning for the computer engineering students. The learning outcome is to persuade the junior students within knowledge of basic electrical and electronics basis for young entrepreneurs. The evaluation shows that students can improve and understand that the basic knowledge of this course is the first step of successful innovation in the future.

articleTitle: Architecture of Artificial Intelligence Entrepreneurship on Digital Ecosystem for Higher Education Institutions
abstract: The objective of this research is to analyze the components of artificial intelligence entrepreneurship on the digital ecosystem for higher education institutions and synthesize the conceptual framework. This will involve the use of documentary research methods to analyze and synthesize the conceptual framework. The findings were that the conceptual framework consists of three components: (1) Business Model, (2) AI-Assisted Business Model, and (3) Ecosystem of Artificial Intelligence Entrepreneurship. It can be applied to digital entrepreneurs, entrepreneurs, start-ups, and students interested in doing business in higher education institutions to develop their artificial intelligence entrepreneurial competencies appropriately and effectively.

articleTitle: A Study of Resilience Profile of Firstyear Students During Hybrid Learning
abstract: Students are facing their own challenges during the transition and adaptation processes in their first year of study. Understanding of their resilience factors is seen as crucial to better understanding their adaptation skills during the firstyear study. This study aims to explore the resilience profile of the first-year students to remain persistent and survive during the transition processes. The Cognitive-Afective-Conative Questionnaire (CACQ) instrument was distributed among first year students involving eight faculties at a Malaysian university. The quantitative data were analysed using Statistical Package Social Science (SPSS) version 22.0, according to the mean score, and standard deviation. The findings found a high level of mean score for the entire students with no-significant differences in the resilient profile across the fields of studies. This study highlights the importance of fostering students’ desire, resourcefulness, initiative, and persistence to ensure study success of students in the context of higher education study.

articleTitle: Development Model of Self-Directed Learning with Digital Content Media to Enhance Electrical Teaching Skills for Students of Teacher Training Program
abstract: The purposes of this research were to: 1) to develop a self-directed learning model combined with digital media to enhance electrical teaching skills for students of teacher training program and 2) to study the results of using a self-directed learning model combined with digital median to enhance electrical teaching skills for students of teacher training program. The Sample groups of the research were 12 Second-year students with a bachelor's degree in the Department of Teacher Training in Electrical Engineering, King Mongkut's University of Technology North Bangkok. The research tools used in this research are 1) Digital media-based learning resources include websites, video media multimedia, and e-textbooks, 2) Electrical teaching skills assessmen form, 3) Satisfaction assessment form. The research results show that 1) the suitability of self-directed learning formats combined with digital media to enhance electrical teaching skills for students of teacher training program is appropriate at a high level. The mean was 4.24 and the standard deviation was 0.49, 2) The assessment results of electrical teaching skills were higher than the set criteria of 80 percent, with an overall mean of 84.33. 3) The students had opinions on the Self-directed learning model combined with digital media to enhance electrical teaching skills for students of teacher training program at a high level. The mean is 4.22 and the standard deviation is 0.48.

articleTitle: Age Estimation from Acetabulum Using Digital Image Processing Techniques in Thai Population
abstract: Age serves as a parameter for discerning individuals from skeletal remains. Within the pelvic bone, the acetabulum region emerges as a viable locus for assessing bone age. Specifically, the porosity of the acetabular fossa exhibits a potential correlation with bone age. Historically, bones have been forwarded to experts for age assessment, a process often cumbersome and impractical for remote locations. However, transmitting bone images is comparatively facile and expeditious, besides being cost-effective. Nowadays, digital media processor contributes a lot to the analysis of medical results. In this study, a proposition is made to employ digital image processing techniques for quantifying bone porosity, thereby facilitating age estimation. The samples of 123 pelvic bones comprised 40 females aged between 36 and 90 years old, and 83 males aged between 40 and 92 years old. Acetabulum color images were captured and subsequently converted into grayscale images. The ratio of dark gray pixels (representing porosity) to light gray pixels (representing bone) was computed alongside the exact age of the specimen. Age estimation equations were derived and applied using statistic ANOVA analysis. The age estimation equations for males and females are as follows: A=2.290P-27.96 for males and A=0.500P+51.48 for females, where A represents the age estimation and P denotes the percent porosity. As the result, a significant relationship between porosity and age was observed in males, whereas such correlation was absent in females. The resultant errors in age estimation varied within a range of 0 to 16 years. Of paramount concern is the cleanliness of the acetabulum area, as it profoundly influences pixel values.

articleTitle: Factors Predicting the Acquisition of Soft Skills Among Students with Learning Disabilities in Vocational Special Education Secondary School

authors.preferredName: Wan Hanim Nadrah binti Wan Muda

abstract: Acquiring soft skills is essential for all students, including those with disabilities, as these skills contribute to personal and professional success. Soft skills are non-technical abilities that enable individuals to work well with others, communicate effectively, and adapt to various situations. Students with disabilities may face unique challenges in developing their soft skills. This research determined the factors affecting the acquisition of soft skills among students with learning disabilities in Vocational Special Education Secondary Schools. Survey research design is a methodological approach used in this study to collect data from samples by administering a questionnaire. This study focuses on soft skills, which consist of seven elements (communication skills, critical thinking and problem-solving skills, teamwork skills, information management and lifelong learning skills, entrepreneurship skills, moral and ethics skills and leadership skills), self-esteem and self-efficacy as variables. Two secondary schools are involved in this study: Vocational Special Education Secondary School Shah Alam, Selangor and Vocational Special Education Secondary School Indahpura, Johor, with a total sample of 52 students. Data analysis revealed that the combination of variables to predict the acquisition of soft skills from self-esteem and self-efficacy was statistically significant. In conclusion, selfesteem and self-efficacy influence the acquisition of soft skills among students with learning disabilities in Vocational Special Education Secondary Schools.

articleTitle: Promoting Entrepreneurial Mindset of Undergraduate Students by using Design Thinking with Cooperative Learning
abstract: Entrepreneurial mindset has been increasingly interested not only in those who desire to run a business but also for individuals who seek success in their career. Therefore, promoting entrepreneurial mindset in undergraduate students is essential for their near future of work after graduation. This study focuses on developing entrepreneurial mindset of undergraduate students through a practical entrepreneurial experience by using design thinking with cooperative learning. A five-week intervention program was then designed to provide the undergraduate students an experience to embrace opportunities, encourage collaboration and communication skills, and be continuous practice, reflection and feedback. Four key skills demonstrated for entrepreneurial mindset consisted of Leadership, Creativity, Customer Understanding, and Business Feasibility. The undergraduate students were then assessed by these competency sets via self and facilitator. The finding revealed that after participation the undergraduate students could significantly improve entrepreneurial mindset, especially in competency of Business Feasibility, Leadership, and Creativity.

articleTitle: The Development of Learning Skills and Innovation of STEM3.0 Education in Autonomous Robotic Control for Secondary School. Thailand
abstract: This research aims to develop learning skills and innovation of STEM3.0 education in autonomous robotic control for secondary school, Thailand, finds achievement test and evaluate satisfaction of training course in learning skills and innovation of STEM3.0 education in autonomous robotic control for secondary school, Thailand. The sample is student who studied science, total 32 students, selected by purposive sampling. The results found that the course of learning skills and innovation of STEM 3.0 education in autonomous robotic control for secondary school has the efficiency at 80.40/86.77, which is higher than the criteria of 75/75. The learning achievement in learning skills and innovation of STEM 3.0 education in autonomous robotic control for secondary school was assess by the pretest and posttest score, the result indicates that the posttest scores are higher than the pretest score at the 0.05 significant level. The satisfaction of learning and innovation skills training course of STEM3.0 education in autonomous robotic control for secondary school has an average score <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$)\overline{x})$</tex> at 4.57 which is the highest level.

articleTitle: Technology and Graphic Design: Building a STEM Education Ecosystem for the Future
abstract: This study investigates STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) with technology and graphic design in creating an advanced educational ecosystem. This research aims to develop a STEM education ecosystem for the future by leveraging technology and graphic design. The study sample includes students, teachers, and education experts in the STEM field, along with tools and resources related to technology and graphic design in education. Sampling methods will involve online surveys, individual and group interviews, as well as direct observations in educational settings. Research tools will encompass data analysis software, IT applications for data collection and processing, and graphic design tools. Data will be analyzed using statistical methods and content analysis to understand the positive impact of integrating technology and graphic design into STEM education. The expected outcome is to provide specific recommendations to enhance the quality of education, foster creativity and exploration in STEM fields, and establish the groundwork for an advanced and future-focused educational environment. The article provides in-depth insights into the development of technological capabilities while emphasizing the crucial role of graphic design in creating a holistic learning environment. A comprehensive approach is proposed in the article to harmoniously combine these elements, providing a plan for developing and implementing an advanced educational ecosystem, preparing learners to face challenges and opportunities in the future. By emphasizing the importance of graphic design in enhancing visual communication skills and solving problems creatively, this article proposes an integrated approach to build a dynamic ecosystem. Education equips learners with new learning methods for the future. Based on current research and practical innovation, the article presents a framework for developing and implementing a sustainable and comprehensive STEM-based education model.

articleTitle: The Needs Analysis of a Learning Framework to Enhance Problem-Solving Skills in IoT Course for Non-Engineer Learners
abstract: This research aims to study the needs and learning preferences of non-engineer learners (learners who do not study engineering majors) to increase problem-solving skills in Internet of Things (IoT) studies and provide a basis for designing new learning frameworks. This research used indepth interviews with 5 non-engineering learners to gather insights into their needs, preferences, and challenges. The interviews were semi-structured and consisted of questions about background information. and open-ended questions about opinions. Thematic analysis was then used to identify repeating patterns from all interview transcripts. The results of the interviews revealed that non-engineering learners have an interest in IoT technology but encounter problems and need to develop problem-solving skills for IoT development, including a lack of knowledge and experience related to IoT, lack of motivation to learn about IoT, finding an IoT solution to solve a real-world problem. Dealing with these problems may be achieved by designing a learning framework that includes active learning techniques with problem-based learning (PBL), gamification, and hands-on learning. to gain experience with IoT hardware and software. However, this research is still in the early stages. More research may validate these findings whether this is related to a larger sample size, various student profiles, or long-term studies to evaluate long-term effects further.

articleTitle: The Integrating Problem-Based Learning with Collaborative Learning to Develop Motivation
abstract: In industrial plants Interns will have a role similar to that of an employee. With a chaperone who is a regular employee Taking care of providing knowledge to students Of course, in working, students are likely to encounter many problems. Therefore, it is essential to develop themselves in various skills and motivation. Integrating problem-based learning with collaborative learning to develop motivation using the concept of a four-step learning framework: problem study, problem solving, summarizing and presenting solutions to problems that arise from learners' experiences or opportunities to face. The learning process will be stimulated, and additional knowledge on the problem will be needed to provide learners with the possibility of finding a solution and motivation to solve it before entering the study stage. Understanding the problem, brainstorming for further solutions. At this stage, students must work together to plan and finalize the problem and present the results of the problem to their potential and effectiveness, and also help them to make future career choices.

articleTitle: Classroom Management as Virtual World for Creating Professional Teaching Environment
abstract: Research and innovation for community or local development, aims at providing the individuals with a high quality of life and enhancing capabilities for competition through collaborative efforts of stakeholders, including beneficiaries in the area, especially the academic sector of which powerful educational institutions in the central and metropolitan areas of Thailand. Innovation in vocational education management through online teaching environments intends to have educational innovations in the central and metropolitan areas as a mechanism and process of educational reform that can manage online teaching in line with the local context. This involves flexible and adaptable management that eliminates the need for travel and reduces consumption of resources. This is achieved by research objective of 1) developing innovations in vocational education management through online teaching environments to enhance educational efficiency, 2) reducing educational quality disparities by designing virtual reality training centers for professional skill development, with a case study in the field of art and design, and 3) developing mechanisms for collaborative education management in the community, through the design and use of application programs to create a professional teaching environment. Therefore, this research and innovation in vocational education management in the central region of Thailand through online teaching environments can enhance self-directed learning. This involves designing and developing learning technology, creating a virtual world to establish a professional teaching environment, and innovating learning application programs from 400 sampling. The education system in this changing crisis has a responsibility to stimulate and revive the grassroots economy after the crisis. This emphasizes the crucial role of education as a continuous tool in building economic and social resilience later.

articleTitle: The Effect of Integrating CDIOS, Case Study and ChatGPT on Problem-Solving Skills: Comparative Study between Experienced and Inexperienced Training Staff
abstract: The development of personnel is crucial for enhancing organizations, particularly in cultivating problemsolving skills. Therefore, the current study aims to establish a systematic process for bolstering problem-solving capabilities and enhance work efficiency. This process incorporates three key theories, including case-based learning, ChatGPT, and the conceive, design, implement and operate (CDIOS Model), with an expanded knowledge store to gather problem solution methods. The process consists of four main steps. The first was reviewing problems using ChatGPT to seek analyzing problems and causes. The second was analyzing problems, exchanging designs to find solutions. Making decision was the third step using ChatGPT to select solutions. The last step was reflecting on results. The sample group comprised 11 bachelor's degree students serving as training staffs. The current results highlighted a strong understanding of issues, particularly in comprehending the problem. When ChatGPT was adapted to assist in problem-solving, the experienced staffs exceled in the design stage. Conversely, the inexperienced staffs demonstrated development in the conceive and design stages by fostering understanding, knowledge sharing, and solution design. In conclusion, ChatGPT proves to be a valuable tool in enhancing problem-solving abilities among training staffs.

articleTitle: Optimization of Electricity Consumption via Peak Time Reallocation: MATLAB Simulation and Arduino based Lab Implementation
abstract: This paper investigates strategies for optimizing electricity usage by reallocating peak demand periods. Various techniques such as dynamic pricing, Demand-Side Management (DSM) and Energy Storage Systems (ESS). The proposed load shifting algorithm based on water filling algorithm is presented along with standard equations, detailed flowchart and tabular data. Implementation of the algorithm via MATLAB simulation for varying scenarios is demonstrated by redistributing the peak loads to off-peak hours by optimal percentages and area segregation. Moreover, a simple version of the algorithm (with on/off) control for three different loads: LED, fan and Elec-tromagnetic latch is demonstrated in laboratory using Arduino microcontroller.

articleTitle: Hill Climbing and Q-Learning on a Ball Balancing System
abstract: Use reinforcement learning to keep a ball centered on a ball and beam system. Show that RL can learn to perform this task. We use a low-cost system that includes a 3D printed housing, a servo-mounted acrylic beam, a time-of-flight laser-ranging sensor, and a conventional table tennis ball. The RL controller serves as a control baseline, with RL agents adjusting its actions to improve system performance based on the angle of the beam, ball position and speed, and current setpoint. Agents use reinforcement learning (RL) techniques. Hill climbing and Q-learning agents were trained, and the running average reward of hill climbing is 31 from running 1000 episodes and Q-learning is 15.5 from running 1000 episodes. Hill climbing and Q-learning algorithms are computationally efficient and valuable in reinforcement learning, despite Q-learning's suboptimal performance in uncertain environments.

articleTitle: Research Trend About Internet of Thing Products in STEM Learning: A Bibliometric Analysis
abstract: This paper aims to elaborate research trends in IoT products for STEM education using a bibliometric method. We use VOSviewer as one of popular software tools for constructing and visualizing bibliometric networks. And, we use Publish or Perish in which it can be effectively integrated with VOSviewer to enhance its capabilities. This study comes from 200 papers collected and selected from the Google Scholar database regarding IoT products for STEM Learning from 2014 to 2024 using co-word and text analysis, then discusses 13 selected articles that have more than 1000 citations. This issue is warm topic that is quite busy being researched in the last decade. The integration of IoT products into STEM education significantly enhances the learning process by providing hands-on, interactive experiences that make complex concepts more tangible and engaging for students.

articleTitle: The Effectiveness of English Grammar Ability through Songs with Think- Pair- Share Technique of Undergraduate Students
abstract: The objectives of this study were 1) to develop lesson plans using English songs with Think-Pair-Share technique based on the 80/80 criteria; 2) to compare the grammar ability before and after learning English grammar through songs with the Think-Pair-Share technique; and 3) to study the student satisfaction towards learning English grammar through songs with Think-Pair-Share technique. It was experimental research using a one-group pre and post test. The sample were 22 third-year students majoring in English Teaching Program at faculty of education, semester 2/ 2023, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya Rajabhat University, by a purposive sampling technique. The research tools were 1) the 5 lesson plans using song activities with Think-Pair-Share technique, 2) the pre-and post test on English grammar, 3) the satisfaction questionnaire through songs with Think-Pair-Share technique, and 4) the In-Depth interview. For the quantitative research, the data were statistically analysed by percentage, mean, and standard deviation (S.D.). The content analysis was conducted by the qualitative research. The findings showed that 1) The song activities enhancing learning English grammar were effective, with scores of 81.96/83.89, exceeding the 80/80 criteria; 2) The students' English grammar ability has been improved after the learning management. The results were statistically significant difference at. 05 level; and 3) The student satisfaction of learning English grammar through songs with Think-Pair-Share technique was at a very high level, with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{X}^{-}=4.75$</tex>, and S.D <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=0.44$</tex>.

articleTitle: Implementing Four Aspects of STEM for Primary Childhood Education in a Robotic Learning Kit
abstract: The essential role of education has proven its im-pact on community development. It starts with early childhood education when it introduces fundamental concepts. Introducing STEM to children is considered to have some challenging aspects. Interest and motivation are two examples of these aspects. As a solution for these aspects, this work proposes an integration concept of STEM by using a robotic learning kit. The learning kit employs a microcontroller with web-based features and robotic sensors to define a specific STEM topic. We adjusted the kit to be compatible with the primary school curriculum in the four STEM aspects. The kit assessment involved a teacher who directly managed a class in the school. The teacher gave a positive signal to the kit.

articleTitle: Vocational Students' Learning Style and Choice of Profession
abstract: In this paper, we have considered whether vocational students' learning style who made their own choice of profession related to their willingness to work in the profession. Students' learning style were identified by Kolb's learning cycles and their correlation with achievement and level of study. We surveyed 158 heavy equipment repairer's students from four Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) schools studying the same Competency-Based Learning curriculum. The study shows that 89.5% of students who chose independently the heavy equipment repairer's profession want to work in their profession, and 84.3% are willing to pursue career development. The dominant learning style of students who chose independently career is “Reflector” (82.7%) while most of respondents are “Reflector” (69.6%).

articleTitle: Automated Academic Service Questions Answering System with Chatbot via LINE OA
abstract: The university enrollment process involves disseminating information about tuition fees, application deadlines, and course prerequisites. Pertinent details, including application forms, semester schedules, and complaint procedures, follow. Post-enrollment information, such as graduation procedures, further educational opportunities, and alumni details, is provided afterward. This process often prompts numerous questions and concerns. Traditionally, interested parties contacted university departments directly, resulting in a high volume of inquiries and delays. To address this, a chatbot capable of handling repetitive tasks from frequently asked questions (FAQs) is proposed. This study develops an automated academic service question answering system via LINE OA, utilizing Dialogflow and LINE developer. Experimental findings reveal that Dialogflow, with machine learning and natural language processing, enables the chatbot to understand conversational content, enhance service efficiency, and accommodate various inquiries, facilitating user access to information through LINE, a widely used chat application in Thailand.

articleTitle: The Implementation of Centrifugal Force in the Geometric Design of Road for Safety Driving Convenience on the Cisarua sta.0+050-1+450
abstract: The road of Cisarua - Ngamprah has winding conditions and can result in accidents from a geometric perspective. Some of the reasons are because the radius, visibility, and pavement widening at bends have inappropriate road slopes. This research aims implementation of centrifugal force in the geometric design of road for safety driving Conveniencet at the Cisarua sta. 0+050 -1+450. This research method uses evaluative and quantitative methods. Data collection is carried out by observing road locations and the agencies responsible for completing geometric traffic data. Data analysis was carried out on centrifugal strength calculation, the highway gradient, arch sharpness calculation, and centrifugal forces implementation on road bends. These actions are lumped through plunging the aftereffect of greater centrifugal force strength. Moreover, this implementation is also able to reduce the chance of accidents due to centrifugal force impacts based on road geometry calculations. Based on the evaluation and implementation of a smaller centrifugal force design, the use of a spiral-circle-spiral bend type with a transition curve can increase safety driving comfort.

articleTitle: Optimizing Course Scheduling Using Unitime Application for STEM Education
abstract: When it comes to STEM education, effective course scheduling is essential since it has a significant impact on both learning outcomes and resource utilization. It is necessary to have modern technological solutions, such as the Unitime application, in order to handle the complexity of course scheduling in an educational environment that is always changing. Within the scope of this intentional study, the application of Unitime in education is investigated, with a particular focus on the potential of Unitime to revolutionize scheduling procedures, enhance stu-dent achievement, and propel institutional efficiency. It makes a contribution to the continuing conversation about the adoption of educational technology and innovation in STEM education by means of case studies and best practices. The method that is utilized in the process of designing a website is a system development life cycle (SDLC) development cycle that utilizes the waterfall approach. In the context of website quality, the ISO/IEC 25010 standard is referred to as “web testing.” When it comes to maintainability testing, compatibility testing, and usability testing, the results that were produced via web testing have fairly good scores.

articleTitle: Clustering Users as Trigger of Twitter Trending Topic Using Pandas Python and SQL Query
abstract: This study aims to analyze trending topic data on Twitter using Python and SQL filters to understand which users trigger and have the most influence on the formation of trending topics. Scalping methods using Node.js, Python, and RapidMiner Studio were used to retrieve data from Twitter with filters based on hashtags and dates. The filtered data was then analyzed using SQL to identify the first users who triggered the trending topics and the users who had the most impact. The results and discussion of this study demonstrate the successful use of scalping methods to retrieve trending topic data on Twitter. The data analysis revealed the users who triggered the trending topics and the users who had the most influence on their formation. The results were visualized through graphs to illustrate trends in tweet volume over time. The conclusion of this study is the successful analysis of trending topic data on Twitter using scalping methods. Recommendations for future research include the development of more automated systems, integration with other social media platforms such as Facebook or Instagram, and further updates to improve the efficiency and relevance of trending topic data analysis on Twitter. This study provides significant benefits in understanding the phenomenon of trending topics on Twitter and offers insights into the users who influence their occurrence.

articleTitle: Development of English Reading Strategies through Collaborative Learning and Blended Learning for English Teaching Program Students, Rajabhat Universities
abstract: To develop the ability in English reading, using reading strategies could support students read more effectively, develop comprehension, and make students read English quickly and effectively. To develop ability of reading, cooperative learning and blended learning could enhance the proficiency with reading skills. The objectives of this study were 1) to study the ability in using reading strategies in English reading of English Teaching Program students and 2) to compare learning achievement of English Teaching Program students before and after using collaborative learning and blended learning. The sampling of this study was 28 first-year students in English Teaching Program, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya Rajabhat University. The research instruments were lesson plans, videos, testes, English critical reading abilities assessment form. The statistics used in this study were Means and Standard Deviation (S.D.). The results of the study showed that the average of the ability in using reading strategies was at good level and learning achievement of English Teaching Program students after using collaborative learning and blended learning was higher than before learning with the statistically significant at the .05 level.

articleTitle: Mapping of Non-Formal Education in Pastry and Bakery Skills in West Java
abstract: This research was conducted in the scope of nonformal education, especially at Course and Training Institutions, Community Learning Activity Centers (PKBM), Learning Activity Studios (SKB), and Foundations in West Java. The aim of this research is to determine the mapping of the categorization of skills fields in non-formal education in West Java and employment in the field of pastry and bakery skills. The method used is quantitative descriptive, the data analyzed is in the form of secondary data, namely the number and type or fields of non-formal educational institutions throughout West Java obtained from the Ministry of Education, Culture, Research and Technology and the Ministry of Manpower. The research results show that there are 228 nonformal educational institutions. There are 31 skill areas, with the most skill areas is in the skills areaFashion Design 15%, Graphic Design 14%, Pastry & Bakery 11%, Bridal Makeup 11% and Computer Engineering 7%. Through the skills acquired, graduates not only find work but also create new jobs, making them contributors in reducing unemployment rates and improving society's welfare through entrepreneurship.

articleTitle: Development and Evaluation of a PANI/PMMA Composite Gas Sensor for Acetone Detection in Breath
abstract: In recent years, the development of sensors capable of detecting acetone levels has garnered attention in health monitoring and personalized medicine. Acetone in the body, a ketone body produced during metabolic processes, has emerged as a promising biomarker for various health conditions, including diabetes, obesity, and metabolic disorders. Its presence in exhaled breath offers a non-invasive means of assessing metabolic health, presenting a unique opportunity for continuous monitoring and early intervention. This research investigated the use of a PANI/PMMA polymer sensor array to measure acetone gas. Breath samples and standard substances (acetone, butyric acid) were collected using a hygienic mask and measured with an electronic nose device. The tests showed the sensor could classify between a blank mask, acetone, butyric acid, and breath odors.

articleTitle: Promoting Computational Thinking Skills Through Game-Based Learning of Students in Lower Secondary School
abstract: This study's objectives were to: 1) compare computational thinking skills before and after game-based learning activities; and 2) study students' satisfaction after game-based learning. The research methodology uses the ADDIE model by driving game-based learning activities and promoting students with computational thinking skills, including decomposition, pattern recognition, abstraction, and algorithm design. The statistical methods used to analyze the data were mean, standard deviation, and t-test. The study's findings revealed that 1) the students' computational thinking skills improved significantly after engaging in game-based learning activities, demonstrating statistical significance at the.05 level, and 2) the overall students' satisfaction after activities with game-based learning was averaged at the highest level (= 4.75, S.D. = 0.52).

articleTitle: Competency of Learning Management through Video on Social Media Platform of Pre-Service Teachers with Collaborative Learning
abstract: Learning management competency is an important component in the development of pre-service teachers who will be practicing in schools. Classroom activity design, instructional media, assessment and evaluation, and student development were all components of learning management. Learning management can be presented in the form of videos on social media. Pre-service teachers can easily generate videos on their smartphones and use a computer tool or application to produce them. In addition, collaborative learning may motivate pre-service teachers to improve their performance through group projects. Working together allows students to exchange knowledge, practice, and eventually develop their work. This study investigates the competency of learning management in producing videos for social media and learning achievements. A simple random sampling included 21 pre-service teachers. The research instruments employed in this study consisted of lesson plans, learning management competency assessment forms, video production abilities assessment forms and test. Mean, standard deviation, and the t-test were utilized in the evaluation. The findings revealed that pre-service teachers who learnt through collaborative learning have a high degree of learning management competency, as well as a high level of video production ability. Learning achievement increased considerably after studying compared to before.

articleTitle: Assessing Knowledge and Understanding of Competency-Based Learning Management through Integrated Contemplative Education of Coaching and Mentoring, and Research-Based Learning
abstract: This research aims to assess knowledge and understanding of competency-based learning management of early childhood education students through integrated contemplative education, coaching and mentoring, and research-based learning. The sample group used in the research was 33 early childhood education students, and the sample was selected by the purposive sampling. They enrolled in the Language and Communication for Early Childhood course and Emotion and Society for Early Childhood course in the second semester of the academic year 2021. Research tools such as integrated contemplative education of coaching and mentoring, research-based learning, teacher characteristics assessment forms, and competency-based learning management knowledge and understanding assessment forms. Research tools are evaluated by experts to evaluate the consistency of expert opinions with the Index of Item-Objective Congruence (IOC), with a mean score of research tools ranging from 0.67 to 1. Data in this study was analyzed using the mean and standard deviation (S.D.). The results of the research found that in terms of Competencies of Early Childhood Education students, in terms of teacher characteristics, students evaluate themselves at a high level (x̄ = 3.28, S.D. = 0.51), which is consistent with teachers evaluating students at a high level as well (x̄ = 3.2 2, S.D. = 0.5 0). In terms of knowledge and understanding of competency-based learning management, students evaluated themselves at a high level (x̄ = 3.20, S.D. = 0.48), which was consistent with teachers’ evaluation of students at a high level as well (x̄ = 3.18, S.D. = 0.42).

articleTitle: Robotic Kinematics Learning Guidance Based on Game Engine Simulation
abstract: This paper investigates the creation processes of robotic kinematics simulation software for educational guidance purposes using a game engine. The game engine, Unity3D, was chosen due to its accessibility, versatility, and built-in real-time rendering. Three functionalities were implemented to showcase common robotic kinematic concepts: Object Coordinates Simulation, Prismatic Kinematic Simulation, and Modified Denavit-Hartenberg Table Simulation. Each simulation allows users to interact with the concepts and visualize their behavior. The objective is to inform the ease of creating educational robotic simulations with free and accessible tools in details, exploring comparison of simulation to traditional lectures or videos as simulation improve the spatial understanding of robotic concepts better as they can be explicitly visualized, and they allow the student to explore and immerse in the content, increasing classroom engagement. They are also inexpensive and maintenance-free compared to practical labs, making them accessible and cost-effective educational tools.

articleTitle: Using Graphic Organizers to Improve STEM Learners' Information Literacy
abstract: This paper was aimed to examine the use of graphic organizers to improve STEM learners' information literacy. The sampling group consisted of two groups of students (engineering and veterinary nursing) in one English course at a private university in Thailand. In each class, students read and drew a graphic organizer after they read a text. Then, they did activities based on their graphic organizers. They also designed their own graphic organizer as their reading project. The findings showed that students found that graphic organizers were suitable and useful for their study with reading texts. However, students tended to rely on only a few types of graphic organizers, particularly flow chart and concept map, due to their convenience in relation to paragraphs of their reading passages.

articleTitle: Development of Tracking and Backward Tracing System for an Automotive Parts Using Optical Character Recognition Technique
abstract: The automotive parts manufacturing industry is fiercely competitive in response to the ever-changing consumer demands. This has led to an increasing diversity of products, it leads to growing difficulties in tracking and tracing defective products back to the manufacturing process. Therefore, this research aims to develop a tracking and backward tracing system for auto-parts products using image sensors to capture product labels on packaging boxes. The captured images will be converted into text using Optical Character Recognition (OCR) technique. Subsequently, the converted data will be integrated into a program to display various packaging statuses on a screen and store packaging data in a database. The results demonstrate the effective usability of the developed system.

articleTitle: The Development of a Blended Learning Management Model with a Project Base Virtual Classroom for Basic Computer Subjects
abstract: The purposes of this research were to: 1) to develop a blended learning management model through project-based virtual classrooms in educational computer program courses., and 2) to study the results of using a blended learning management model through project-based virtual classrooms in educational computer programming courses. The research uses a purposive sampling selection, the sample groups of the research were 15 Second-year students with a bachelor's degree in Teacher Training in the Electrical Engineering Department, at King Mongkut's University of Technology North Bangkok. the data analysis by descriptive statistics such as mean, standard deviation and inference statistics via using t-test. The research tools used in this research are: 1) Virtual classrooms used for online learning, 2) Achievement tests 3) Project assessment forms for Basic Computer Subjects, and 4) Satisfaction Assessment. The research results show that 1) the efficiency of the blended learning management model through project-based virtual classrooms had the efficient of 80.26/81.67 higher than the 80/80 criteria., 2) the learning achievement of students after studying is significantly higher than before studying at a statistically significant level of .01. 3) the students’ satisfaction with the blended learning management model was at a high level (M=4.43, SD.=0.63) and 4) the evaluation results of students’ basic computer work development were higher than the established threshold of 80 percent.

articleTitle: Exploring Thai Engineering Students’ Perceived Attitudes Toward Intercultural Competence in Internship Abroad: A Pre-Study Perspective
abstract: Existing research has focused heavily on how internship experiences increase engineering students’ employment opportunities, their transition to new roles of early-career engineers in the workplace, their perception of engineering and their motivation to study engineering. Arguably, the importance of acquiring knowledge and skills in communicating effectively and appropriately with those from different cultures has been neglected in engineering education research. To address a research gap, this qualitative preliminary study aims to explore Thai engineering students’ attitudes toward intercultural competence as a result of their internship programs abroad. The findings offer new insights into Thai engineering students’ attitudes of openness, which finally help promote mutual understanding and appreciation of cultural differences. The study has a range of implications for considering organizing a pre-arrival orientation for Thai engineering students before their departure. This study also offers suggestions for further research into including intercultural competence in engineering education in different countries.

articleTitle: The Development of Competencies-Based Curriculum in Solar Cell Installation System According to the National Labor Skill Standard in the Field of Solar System Installers, Level 1
abstract: The purpose of this research was to create a develop a competency-based curriculum in solar cell installation system according to the national labor skill standard in the field of solar system installers, Level1, Performance test a curriculum development using <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{E}_{1}/\mathrm{E}_{2}$</tex> with efficiency set to 85/85 and performance test of the solar cell system installation of students in electrical engineering and education field. The media prepared contains a training document entitled “Installation of the power generation system with solar cells on the roof.” Presentation slide and video media kits. This research organizers began to study information on creating a competency-based curriculum package. Then designed and built a training package. The training document consists of four learning units, 1) Fastening safety equipment for working at heights job, 2) Preparation before installing a solar cell system job, 3) Work on installing a solar cell system job, and 4) Solar cell system installation inspection job. Then, we designed and created a series of 11 video learning materials, including 4 slides for training, and created two training manuals: 1) Teacher's Manual and 2) Trainee's Manual After the training package has been prepared, it has been sent to 5 experts for evaluation. The results of the research found that the efficiency value of the competency-based curriculum was 85.91/86.18. The students who participated in the sample of 60 received individual training and work with an average score of 84.75 points and passed the mocking exam with 100 %.

articleTitle: Approaching Vietnamese Folktale Culture Through 3D Scanning Simulation
abstract: Cultural beliefs in Vietnam play a crucial role in perception and serve as the foundation for shaping the cultural identity of each individual. However, due to various reasons, very few students have the opportunity to explore or learn about Vietnam's folk cultures. The aim of this research is to help students understand cultural values within the folk world through the use of 3D scanning technology directly on their smartphones. Using 3D technology, students can scan and engage in interactive experiences with vivid images of folk tales, allowing them to learn and comprehend the historical and cultural significance of folk history or extract valuable lessons from the stories. Through this approach, folk culture becomes more accessible and tangible, fostering evaluation and awareness from the perspective of students. Lastly, it emphasizes the importance of utilizing mobile technology to preserve and promote the diverse and rich imagery of folk culture in the digital age.

articleTitle: Implementing Overflow Warning Systems in Provincial Waterworks Authority Phetchaburi
abstract: The overflow warning device provides a highly effective solution for monitoring and preventing water tank overflows. This study examines the device's performance and impact using data from three tables. The device demonstrated consistent 100% efficiency across ten trials at different distances of 5 cm, 10 cm, and 15 cm, ensuring accurate detection and alerting of overflow situations. It significantly reduced the frequency of tank overflow incidents, completely eliminating them. Additionally, the paper highlights high satisfaction among 10 waterworks employees, who found the device to be more efficient than traditional methods. The device helps minimize the time required to check for overflowing water levels and reduces energy consumption during water production. These findings suggest that the overflow warning device is a reliable and efficient tool for improving operational efficiency and energy savings in water supply systems, contributing to enhanced water management practices.

articleTitle: Analysis of Electroencephalogram Data Activity During Reading Using Scanning and Survey Question Read Recite Review Techniques
abstract: Effective reading techniques are crucial for enhancing comprehension and training the brain to process information efficiently, motivating students to succeed academically. This quantitative experimental study investigates the relationship between test scores and Electroencephalogram (EEG) activity using Scanning and Survey-Question-Read-Recite-Review (SQ3R) reading techniques. Five subjects, all Electrical and Electronics Technical Education students, participated in the study. The research involved four steps, utilizing the OpenBCI EEG Headband Kit and OpenBCI GUI software for real-time data collection. Analysis revealed that three subjects showed higher effectiveness with the Scanning technique, while two favored the SQ3R technique. The findings indicate a correlation between each reading technique's evaluation scores and EEG data. This study provides insights that can help students optimize their learning strategies and reading techniques to achieve academic success.

articleTitle: A Study and Application of Fire Alarm System in Computer and Telecommunication Control Room
abstract: The Study and application of fire alarm system in computer and telecommunication control room aims to study and design the design of an emergency notification system in the control room along with testing and implementation.
