The system is designed for fire incident detection and alarm notifications by utilizing electronic devices and micro controllers as tools for fire incident detection such as smoke and heat generation and notify involved personnel before a fire occurs, using the principles of electronic equipment integrated with the Internet of things for signal transmission and installation testing in building premises. During testing, the system can rapidly send emergency notifications when incidents occur on-site, and able to notify via the LINE application, providing users with timely awareness of impending fire incidents. This is highly beneficial as it allows users to quickly check the alerted areas and prepare for incident mitigation before any damage occurs to personnel and property in the building. The test results show that the signal transmission aspect of the system works well with the emergency notification devices, and the system operates according to the programmed conditions accurately with high satisfaction from users and personnel involved in building management at a significantly high level.

Author Keywords: Fire alarm system; Microcontroller; Application notification

articleTitle: Developing English Pronunciation through Social Media Platform by using Flipped Classroom and Cooperative Learning of Computer Education Students
abstract: To investigates the efficacy of flipped classroom and cooperative learning approaches in enhancing English pronunciation among Computer Education students at Rajabhat University. Given the global nature of the tech industry, effective communication in English is crucial. However, traditional teaching methods often fail to address the specific pronunciation needs of non-native English speakers. Flipped classroom and cooperative learning were conducted in this study. The purposes of this study were 1) to study the ability in English pronunciation through social media platform by using flipped classroom and cooperative learning of Computer Education students 2) to study the ability in producing VDO social media platform by using flipped classroom and cooperative learning of Computer Education students and 3) to compare learning achievement of Computer Education students before and after learning with flipped classroom and cooperative learning. The sampling group were the 28 Computer Education second-year students who enrolled English for Computer in the first semester 2023. The research instruments were consisted of lesson plans, pre-test and post-test, the ability in pronunciation assessments. The statistics used in this research were Means, Standard Deviation (S.D.) and t-test. The results indicated that 1) the ability in pronunciation was at high level (M= 3.75, S.D. 0.60) 2) the ability in producing VDO social media platform by using flipped classroom and cooperative learning of Computer Education students was at high level and 3) learning achievement of the students after learning by using flipped classroom and cooperative learning was higher than before learning at statistical significance

articleTitle: The Development of Information Systems to Enhance Students' Punctuality and Responsibility
abstract: Responsibility in learning is an important characteristic. However, students nowadays may not know how to manage their time properly with the tasks they need to complete, it results in an overload of work, causing stress and affecting their studies. Therefore, the current research aims to develop and test the information system in promoting students' punctuality and responsibility behavior. The sample group consisted of 37 high school students in Thailand. In the information system used for the research, a website was developed featuring key functions such as an activity-log system and an attendance time system. Research tools included questionnaire on satisfaction in using the information system, named ForSchool website, questionnaire on the efficiency of using the ForSchool website, and student responsibility assessment form. Research findings indicated that using activity logs as an effective tool enhanced responsibility and punctuality, helping students manage their time efficiently and complete their tasks on schedule. The information system in promoting students' punctuality and responsibility behavior yielded high satisfaction.

articleTitle: Using Project-Based Learning to Enhance Scientific Process Skills for Grade 11 Students
abstract: The purposes of this research were 1) to study scientific process skills using project-based learning for grade 11 students 2) to compare learning achievement before and after studying with project-based learning. The sample groups used in this research were grade 11 students at the demonstration school of Rajabhat Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya University by random sampling. The research tools were project-based learning lesson plans, science process skills assessment form and learning achievement tests. Statistics used in this research were percentage, means, standard deviation and t-test. The results of this research found that 1) grade 11 students who studied with project-based learning had high levels of scientific process skills. 2) learning achievement of grade 11 students after studying was higher than before studying with statistical significance at the .05 level.

articleTitle: Schizotypy, Manual Dexterity, and Cognitive Ability Distinguish STEM and Non-STEM Students
abstract: The neuroscience of education is an approach to the scholarship of learning and teaching that draws on cognitive and brain sciences. It holds potential for enhancing pedagogical understanding, such as the variation between students in terms of ability. One such example is schizotypy, a personality trait that is linked to neurodevelopmental disorders, cognitive weaknesses, and relatively low academic performance. Schizotypy has been reported to be lower in STEM students compared, to other groups, particularly arts students. But less is known about cognitive ability variations between students in different majors. We compared three groups of university students, studying STEM, arts, or social science. All were evaluated with a self-report measure of schizotypy, and a battery of tests focused on cognitive, social cognition, and motor skill. The results confirmed that the study groups did indeed vary on schizotypy and task performance. Contrary to expectations, STEM students were found to be relatively high on positive aspects of schizotypy, scoring higher on the cognitiveperceptual subscale than non-STEM students, and they also scored below non-STEM students on a perceptual task. We also observed associations between schizotypy and performance measures across the full sample. Specifically, students with more negative schizotypy, scoring relatively high on the interpersonal subscale, had significantly better executive function (switching) and significantly worse manual dexterity. We conclude that schizotypy (as a form of neurodiversity), cognitive ability, and motor dexterity, may be important factors linked to selection of study major among university students, which has implications for their educational achievements.

articleTitle: Strengthen Teaching Skills for 21st-Century in Thailand's Remote Area Using Design Thinking
abstract: The drastic changes, coupled with the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, remote areas have faced challenges in accessing learning and developing science, technology, and digital skills, especially in the education sector. The educational system in remote areas of Ratchaburi is confronting various obstacles. These include a shortage of qualified teachers, inadequate support for teachers, an irrelevant curriculum, and a lack of integration of 21st-century skills. Addressing these challenges necessitates a comprehensive approach that emphasizes teacher professional development programs, governance support, and the promotion of innovative teaching and learning methods adapted to the specific needs of remote areas. Our findings indicate that the use of design thinking can significantly enhance teachers' abilities to promote 21st-century skills in remote areas. The teacher-led activity using a design-thinking approach yielded impressive results, leaving both educators and students feeling proud and motivated. The students' enthusiastic participation and ability to reflect on their work displayed positive outcomes and skills introduced by the teacher's encouragement and the application of the 4Cs framework. Furthermore, the activity served as a source of inspiration for teachers, motivating them to develop their teaching techniques and incorporate similar activities into their curriculum.

articleTitle: Introducing Secondary School Students to Telecommunications Engineering Through the WiFinder Project: Part II –Training Workshop
abstract: Secondary school is an important period for students to consider numerous career options. Students can obtain exposure to a variety of STEM (science, technology, engineering, and mathematics) professions by learning about engineering ideas. This exposure will allow them to make more informed decisions about their future academic and professional endeavors. Introducing engineering principles to secondary school students is therefore critical. Recent literature highlights that numerous STEM activities related to engineering have centered around robotics, the Internet of Things, or drones. The WiFinder project was initiated to introduce an activity in telecommunications engineering as an alternative. This work reports the promotion of Telecommunications Engineering concepts to secondary schools in various parts of Thailand. The key part was accomplished through the WiFi signal sources locating tool along with the activities design. These activities allowed students to develop a broad theoretical understanding of telecommunications engineering. Primary topics included radio transmitters and receivers, antenna theory, transmission lines, and wave propagation. This workshop was designed to transfer and boost that knowledge to teachers/educators, and student leaders. Since the outset, 1,147 educational institutions have applied to participate in this training session. Among those, 243 institutions participated in the training workshop. A total of 502 handheld kits were distributed during the training. Pre- and post-training assessments of teachers/educators and students showed an average improvement of 34.04%. The participants indicated positive feedback during the workshop, especially the hands-on activities. The future lesson adoption or integration into the curriculum may depend on schools’ acceptance and preferred pedagogical approaches.

articleTitle: At the Intersection of Service Learning and Engineering Education for Sustainable Development: A Bibliometric Review of Research (2004–2023)
abstract: Over the past two decades, service learning has become increasingly prominent in engineering education for sustainable development. Nonetheless, a comprehensive review of research in this field has been lacking. This bibliometric review aims to fill this gap by analyzing 131 Scopus-indexed documents spanning from 2004 to 2023. The descriptive analysis uncovered a growing body of literature, with a predominant contribution from the United States. Citation analyses further identified influential scholars, institutions, and sources, enhancing our understanding and advancing knowledge in this domain. The keyword cooccurrence analysis highlighted key topics and conceptual foci, including project-based learning, ethics and social responsibility, graduate education and research, capstone courses, and first-year engineering. Additionally, the study identified research fronts in areas such as learning outcomes, multidisciplinary teamwork, renewable energy, and food security.

articleTitle: Development of Game-Based Learning on Personal Income Tax Literacy and Mathematical Decision Making for Strategic Tax Planning
abstract: This study introduces Tax Master, a board game designed to enhance tax literacy through strategic and interactive learning. By incorporating practical applications of mathematics and financial decision-making, the game addresses the educational gap in tax literacy and offers an engaging approach to learning taxation. Utilising real-world financial scenarios, Tax Master provides players with a deep understanding of personal income tax systems, tax deductions, and strategic financial planning. The game's dual phase design caters to both foundational tax education and advanced competitive scenarios, encouraging players to apply their knowledge in a simulated environment that mirrors real-life financial management. This innovative educational tool promises to revolutionise the way tax literacy is taught, making it more relevant, engaging, and effective for learners of all ages.

articleTitle: Integrating CDIO and Problem Based Learning Frameworks for Industrial Internet of things Training Course Development
abstract: Industrial sector has shifted from traditional to more advanced industries, focusing on integrating technology and developing skills to enhance productivity. Previous studies highlighted that the CDIO approach was suitable for technical training but faced complexity, time constraints, and challenges in adapting to the needs of learners and instructors. This paper proposed a new learning model that tackled these issues by integrating problem-based learning, using real learner problems as the foundation for skill development. This model was applied in training for Internet of Things education in the industrial sector, combining app-based learning with practical training. It began with identifying learner needs through group discussions, followed by curriculum design and app-supported theoretical learning, culminating in practical exercises. Results showed that this model simplified curriculum development, enhanced adaptability, and reduced learning time, increasing learning efficiency by up to 71.43 percent. While learners were satisfied and engaged, further skills such as programming and platform usage needed development. Flexibility and ongoing teaching innovation are crucial for the CDIO model to meet current and future workforce needs.

articleTitle: Rethinking Learning Media and ICT Literacy Courses for Future Vocational Teachers: Ensuring Quality in Learning Media
abstract: In the context of tewnty first century vocational education, educators are increasingly tasked with mastering the skills of learning media development. Prospective vocational teachers are provided with learning media and ICT literacy courses. This research aims to explore the correlation and impact between academic performance in learning media courses and the subsequent quality, productivity, and variety of the produced learning media of 38 prospective vocational teacher. The study employed a correlational analysis to investigate the relationship between academic grades and the outcomes of the learning media development process. Result showed lack of correlation between academic scores in learning media courses and the quality and quantity of learning media production reveals the intricate challenge of aligning theoretical understanding with practical skills. Academic scores only have an impact on the number of variations in learning media because the focus of the course is to introduce various types of learning media. Reflection is offered to enhance and evaluate the learning media and ICT literacy courses. This research is useful for universities producing vocational teachers as a reference for future curriculum improvements.

articleTitle: Teaching STEAM and Engineering Education Through Project-Based Learning: Fostering Creativity and Innovation in Students
abstract: Teaching STEAM Education and Engineering through Project-Based Learning fosters creativity and innovation among Grade 12 students. The approach involves a structured process with six steps, initiating with problem identification and the collection of information and concepts related to the problem. Subsequently, students move on to the design phase, followed by testing, evaluation, and revision of the solution or workpiece, encapsulated in the stages of Testing, Evaluation, and Design Improvement. The final step culminates in the presentation of solutions. This problem-solving and presentation approach is organized according to the study stream concept, incorporating the engineering design process. The research model employed is classroom action research at Sarasas Witaed Rangsit School, Thailand, during the first semester of the academic year 2023, involving a total of 123 students. The findings demonstrate that the stream-based learning approach, coupled with the engineering design process, effectively stimulates the creativity and innovation of Grade 12 students. Notably, teachers are advised to emphasize the significance of critical situations by introducing challenging conditions for students. The students' analytical skills are evident as they assess the context through brainstorming, design various pieces, plan the implementation process, select appropriate testing methods, evaluate their workpieces, make improvements, and ultimately present and refine their own creations. The results highlight continuous development in students’ creativity and innovation. The most prominent behavioral expression observed throughout the learning process is creative collaborative behavior, while the least expressed behavior is openness and courage to explore.

articleTitle: Welding Technology Students’ Perception on the Use of Google Classroom Application at Vocational College
abstract: Google classroom (GC) is one of the online applications that can be used to replace face-to-face learning environment. GC offers many benefits to users, such as userfriendliness, free of charge, and accessible at everywhere and in every time. Nonetheless, it also comprises disadvantages as its utilization requires stable internet connection and teacher's competency in ICT and online pedagogy. Therefore, this study was conducted to identify the students’ perceptions on the use of GC in terms of its effectiveness, student personality formation and students’ satisfaction from the perspective of Vocational College students. A total of 103 Diploma Students in Welding Technology at a Vocational College were invited to participate in this study. Questionnaire which contained 22 items was used in this study. The findings indicate that the students were highly satisfied with the use of GC in learning. Conversely, they perceived that GC was only moderately effective for learning and to nurture students’ personality. These findings suggest that teachers should improve their ICT skill and online pedagogical skills in order to create an effective learning environment for students. Additionally, meaningful learning activities that embed positive values should be thoroughly designed and implemented to nurture students’ personalities.

articleTitle: A Bibliometrics Analysis of Online Learners' Self-Regulation in Higher Education Using Biblioshiny
abstract: This study analyzes the growth of self-regulation and online learning in higher education using bibliometrics. The findings show a significant increase in these topics since 2019, indicating continuity. The keywords have evolved into more diversified, multidisciplinary themes that suggest a complex connection between these topics. The study also highlights the increasing interest in interdisciplinary research. The central theme, higher education, is deeply related to self-regulation, online learning, and Covid-19. The major contributors are China, the USA, Germany, and Australia. This study's theoretical implications offer a general overview of the literature on online learning and self-regulation, with practical implications for researchers, educators, and students. Future bibliometric analyses could include new search terms and multiple databases to get more well-rounded perspectives and a more comprehensive review.

articleTitle: The Overview of Higher Vocational School Teachers' Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Competency: A Preliminary Study from Bibliometric Review and the Perspective of Teachers and Students
abstract: In the context of the digital economy, information and communication technology (ICT) competency is a crucial 21st-century competency for higher vocational school (HVS) teachers to cultivate digital talent. However, research on the ICT competency of HVS teachers in China is still underdeveloped. This study aims to identify research gaps in this field for further research. Through this bibliometric analysis, researchers identified that there is limited research on undergraduate level vocational schools (ULVS) teacher. Subsequently, semi-structured interviews were conducted with ULVS teachers and students in Guangdong Province, China, to understand their perspectives on teachers’ ICT competency and its framework development. The study concludes that developing an appropriate ICT competency framework among ULVS teachers is urgently needed.

articleTitle: A Study on Japanese-Style STEAM Practices about “Paper” for Early Childhood Education Focusing on the Sustainability Competencies
abstract: In Japan, interest in STEAM education, which adds an “A” to STEM, has grown recently. The point of Japanese-style STEAM is that the “A” is not limited to the arts but includes a broad range of liberal arts, such as life, economics, etc. The background to the interest in STEAM education is the international focus on sustainability competencies for realizing such as SDGs. Early childhood education in Japan has long been conducted as a well-rounded education. Thus, by reviewing its value, we may obtain essential clues regarding developing sustainability competencies that will be newly required for global early childhood education. This study examined four Japanese-style STEAM education practices about “paper” for young children from the perspective of UNESCO's eight key competencies for sustainability [1]. As a result, it was found that though it is not explicitly shown in the Course of study for Kindergarten, learning about environmental issues, sustainability, ecology, ecosystems, etc., and support for developing sustainability competencies were already in place. On the other hand, however, these practices are still dependent on the competencies of individual early childhood educators, and it became clear that systematic curriculum building based on good practices and teacher training are issues to be addressed.

articleTitle: Exploring Demographic Disparities in the Mastery of Higher-Order Thinking Skills among Primary School Pupils
abstract: Today's pupils should cultivate higher-order thinking skills (HOTS) more than anything else. This study aims to assess the HOTS level among primary school pupils based on demographics and their differences. The population in this study included all Year 5 pupils at primary school in Malacca. Malaysia. A total of 73 pupils from a primary school in Malacca, Malaysia were selected as research samples. The SEA test (Synthesis, Evaluation and Analysis) was modified to collect research findings. Data were analyzed descriptively and inferentially using SPSS software and presented into mean, frequency, and percentage. The findings showed that most primary pupils have a very low level of HOTS based on gender and socioeconomics (SES). T-test analysis showed that there was no significant difference in the mean scores of HOTS level between male and female pupils. However, there was a significant difference in the mean scores of HOTS level based on SES. In conclusion, to support pupils' HOTS abilities, the HOTS instruction should cultivate reasoning and problem-solving techniques rather than procedural fluency.

articleTitle: Build Up the Sustainable Talent Ecosystem: An Empirical Study of Taiwan AITalent Demand Survey
abstract: The study aims to investigate the current state of AI applications in the Taiwanese information service industry and AI startups through a questionnaire. It delves into the present and future demand for AI talent in these sectors. The study also seeks to identify innovative training methods based on survey results to address the shortage of AI talent. The survey findings indicate that with the emergence of generative AI (GAI) and the maturation of AI technologies, the trend in AI usage is shifting towards vertical applications and productization. As a result, there is an increasing demand for application-oriented and interdisciplinary AI talent. It is crucial to develop suitable approaches to equip the workforce with AI skills and establish a reliable talent certification mechanism to promote the widespread adoption of AI.

articleTitle: FairyS: Development of a board game integrated elements of Vietnamese folklore
abstract: With the development of technology and society, the creation of electronic devices, media, and social networks has opened a new era and been a great step forward. This means that Vietnamese fairy tales, folktales, and legends sought after by children through books, radio, and especially through the loving and emotional stories of grandparents in ancient society have gradually disappeared. The FairyS board game set is inspired by characters from Vietnamese folk culture, imbued with the unique identities of Vietnamese fairy tales, folk tales, and legends. It helps players connect with cultural knowledge through game experiences. This study explains the process of integrating elements of Vietnamese folk culture into the design of the FairyS board game. Research will contain two main objectives. Firstly, explain the exploitation of elements of Vietnamese folklore and their integration into the design of the FairyS board game. Secondly, discuss the experiences of players in integrating Vietnamese folklore into the FairyS board game. A survey of 110 students from high school to college was conducted for this study, and 10 of them were selected for in-depth interviews. The results show that Vietnamese folk culture elements integrate designs as well as player experiences based on the four user experience factors mentioned that are agreed upon and appreciated. The study found that integrating Vietnamese folk culture elements into game design can not only help players entertain and develop soft skills, but also help them access cultural knowledge quickly.

articleTitle: Critical Thinking Skill Enhancement with ECDIO Model in Electronics Industry
abstract: In the industry, defects and rejected work pieces pose significant challenges in the electronics sector, impacting product quality, production efficiency, and company reputation. These problems were solved by employees. Therefore, training is important for enhancing employees' performance. This paper focuses on improving employees' critical thinking skills through the ECDIO model. There are five steps involved in the learning process: E: Engagement, C: Conceive, D: Design, I: Implementation, and O: Operation. The results revealed that the employees had higher critical thinking skills. Moreover, the study's findings underscored the positive impact of the ECDIO model on employees' critical thinking skills. The systematic approach guided the employees from comprehending the problem to leveraging it for perceptive inquiry. Subsequently, they analyzed the problem, discerning its root causes by considering relevant variables, and then proceed to devise effective solutions. Furthermore, the model made it easier for them to apply the knowledge, which they acquired during training to solve actual problems that came up at work every day.

articleTitle: Barriers to Students' Access to Stem Education in the Education System in Vietnam
abstract: The necessity of STEM education (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) is becoming increasingly undeniable in the educational systems of many countries, seen as a crucial driving force for economic and technological development. Applying STEM education to the education system will encourage innovation in problemsolving skills and critical thinking among students, but the actual implementation poses many difficulties and challenges, especially for students in the education system in Vietnam.Using appropriate research methods, this study focuses on analyzing and evaluating the barriers to students' access to STEM education in Vietnam. The study identifies several main barriers to STEM education, including limitations in educational resources, lack of academic support, bias and discrimination, soft skills and personal development, along insufficient career information and guidance. By elucidating these barriers, the results of the study will provide information to policymakers, teachers, and stakeholders about the challenges that students face when accessing STEM education in the Vietnamese education system. Concurrently, this study makes a significant contribution towards fostering a just and excellent STEM educational atmosphere, guaranteeing equal opportunities for every pupil to participate in STEM education.

articleTitle: Construction and Practice of PBL Teaching Model of Mechatronics Training Course for International Students in Higher Vocational Colleges based on STEM
abstract: With the deepening of education reform, traditional teacher-lead instruction has been gradually replaced by new teaching methods. As a new concept of global engineering education, STEM has become a hot spot of academic attention. Based on the concept of STEM, this paper constructs a PBL (Project Based Learning) teaching model for the course of mechatronics training for international higher vocational students. The model is composed of the target layer, preparation layer, implementation layer and guarantee layer, and takes the manipulator handling project as an example to carry out the implementation. In the process of project-based learning, students take the initiative to construct knowledge and focus on applying what they know to solve authentic problems, their knowledge transfer, engineering thinking, scientific literacy, collaborative innovation, and other advanced abilities are effectively cultivated. A multiple evaluation system consisting of self-evaluation, mutual evaluation and teacher evaluation has been established. As a result, PBL teaching model based on STEM could be an effective means of teaching training courses, and it can be successfully employed with students who have ever been exposed and subjected to a background of traditional forms of teaching and learning. After the course implementation, students’ learning investment has increased significantly, their comprehensive ability has been greatly improved, and their learning satisfaction was high.

articleTitle: Current and Emerging Trends in Python Programming Learning
abstract: Programming skills are very important in the rapidly changing technological landscape of the modern world. Due to its versatile features, Python has been widely used in developing applications for modern computing devices. However, learners face challenges in finding appropriate learning paths and content among the frequently disorganized and varied contents available for learning Python. This article aims to help such learners find courses that best fit their unique requirements and learning goals by offering a clear and simple roadmap. The research presented in this article examines pedagogical approaches used by some of the popular institutions offering courses in Python. It also emphasizes the importance of websites as helpful resources for prospective Python learners. The article aims to provide a set of organized resources for those starting their Python programming adventure while keeping up with emerging trends in Python education by carefully analyzing various resources. The ultimate goal of the article is to provide students with the information and knowledge required to successfully traverse the evolving world of Python programming.

articleTitle: Echoes of Tradition: Virtual-Reality Media in Improving Spatial Space Experience 3D Virtual Tour of Kampung Adat Pulo Garut, West Java, Indonesia
abstract: In the current digital era, virtual reality (VR) technology is rapidly expanding across various fields, including education and cultural preservation. This technology offers immersive opportunities to explore and experience architectural spaces, promising increased understanding and learning motivation. Despite being relatively new in Indonesia, the application of VR has shown significant potential for education and cultural preservation through the implementation of a 3D virtual tour in Kampung Adat Pulo Garut. Therefore, this research aimed to develop VR media to enhance users' spatial experience and preserve the cultural values of Kampung Adat Pulo Garut through interactive learning. The method used was Research and Development (R&D) through the Multimedia Development Life Cycle (MDLC) model. The equipment used was LiDAR Scanner FJD Trion P1 Series, DJI Mavic Air 2S Drone, and Sony A6000 Camera. The method used included aerial and terrestrial mapping, 3D modeling, and the development of virtual environments through Unreal Engine. The developmental process included various stages, namely concept, design, material collection, compilation, testing, and distribution. The result showed an interactive 3D virtual tour of Kampung Adat Pulo Garut, called “Echoes of Tradition.” Unreal Engine was found to enable detailed visualization of traditional architecture and village environments with high accuracy and interactivity. The final product offered an immersive learning experience, enriching users' experience, and enabling digital preservation of cultural heritage. The next step, to get an overview of the research results, used a questionnaire as an instrument which was distributed to a total of 250 respondents. Furthermore, the potential implication of VR in education and cultural preservation was identified, guiding similar applications in the future. By improving accessibility and engagement in spatial and cultural learning, VR offered new avenues in education and cultural preservation in Indonesia.

articleTitle: Empowering Architectural STEM Education: Unveiling Student Experiences Through Virtual Reality (VR) in Building Information Modeling (BIM) Course
abstract: The Architectural Engineering Education (AEE) Program faces challenges in incorporating digital tools such as BIM due to limited resources and traditional teaching methods. Virtual Reality (VR) offers a promising solution to enhance the learning experience by immersing students in virtual environments, enabling deeper understanding and hands-on engagement with architectural concepts. This study explores the utilization of VR technology to enhance the learning experience in Building Information Modeling (BIM) courses within the AEE program at Universitas Pendidikan Indonesia. Focusing on student responses after being equipped with low-end VR devices, the research aims to understand the effectiveness of VR technology as a pedagogical tool in STEM-based architecture. Employing a quantitative-qualitative research design, data was collected from 55 students through structured questionnaires and thematic analysis of open-ended responses. The findings reveal predominantly positive perceptions of VR's impact on learning, including enhanced interest, enjoyment, understanding, and recommendation for VR usage. However, challenges such as motion sickness and language proficiency barriers were identified. Positive feedback highlights VR's benefits in fostering engagement, visualization, and teamwork, while negative feedback underscores the need for better preparation, device accessibility, and technical support. Overall, the study underscores VR's potential to revolutionize BIM education while emphasizing the importance of addressing associated challenges for optimal integration and enhanced learning outcomes.

articleTitle: A Data-Driven Design Module Development for Enhancing Multi-Attribute Decision-Making (MADM) Efficacy
abstract: The development of decision-making modules that leverage data-driven design principles is crucial for enhancing the efficacy of multi-attribute decision-making (MADM) systems. This paper discussed modules, focusing on the integration of diverse attributes into the decision-making process. Five distinct modules are proposed within this framework, each tailored to address specific aspects of MADM, thereby offering a compre- hensive approach to decision support. The proposed modules are conceptualized based on a thorough analysis of existing data- driven design methodologies and MADM theories, ensuring their relevance and applicability to real-world decision-making scenar- ios. The effectiveness and validity of the proposed framework and its modules are assessed through expert reviews. These reviews involve subject matter experts evaluating the content structure, usability, and applicability of the modules in various decision- making contexts. The feedback obtained from these reviews is integral to refining the modules, ensuring their alignment with the needs and expectations of end-users. For practitioners, the framework provides a structured approach to developing decision-making modules that are both robust and adaptable, capable of accommodating a wide range of decision attributes. For researchers, it offers a conceptual and methodological foun- dation for further exploration into data-driven design and its application in MADM. This paper contributes to the evolving field of decision support systems, highlighting the importance of structured content development in enhancing the decision- making capabilities of organizations and individuals alike.

articleTitle: Using Machine Learning Models to Evaluate and Predict STEM Postgraduates' Graduation Rates: A Case Study of China
abstract: This article aims to use graduation rate data to fit a machine learning model, understand which attributes influence the graduation rate, and predict the graduation rate. The data collection scope includes four independent variables related to graduation rates in 14 subjects of Chinese postgraduates from 2002 to 2022: Total number of doctoral and master's graduates that year, Total number of doctoral and master's Students entrants that year, Total number of doctoral and master's students enrolment that year, Estimated Graduates for Next Year Total. This study assesses five regression models: Linear, Ridge, Support Vector Regression (SVR), Decision Tree, and Gradient Boosting, using metrics such as MSE, RMSE, MAE, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{R}^{2}$</tex>, and K-Fold CV RMSE. Gradient Boosting emerges as the top performer with the lowest MSE (155.976), RMSE (12.489), and MAE (7.494), and the highest <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{R}^{2}$</tex> (0.622). It shows robust generalization with a K-Fold CV RMSE of 12.272. In contrast, models like Decision Tree and SVR exhibit significant discrepancies and higher prediction errors. Therefore, Gradient Boosting is the most effective model for predicting graduation rates in subjects like Science, Engineering, Agriculture, and Medicine.

articleTitle: A Module for Infusion High Order Thinking Skills (iHots) into Measurement and Geometric Among form One Students
abstract: One highly important ability for overcoming challenges in today's world is Higher Order Thinking talent (HOTS), particularly in the field of mathematics. therefore, the research conducted in the mathematics subject can improve by utilizing infusion Higher Order Thinking Skill (iHOTS) modules. A planning framework has been created using the four core competencies and overall competencies found in the revised Bloom's Taxonomy, which are also the main building blocks found in HOTS. Analyze, apply, evaluate, and create comprise the HOTS construct. A sample of the research involved 120 first-grade pupils from four different schools in the state of Johor. Data is gathered utilizing research decision tests pre- and post-testing before and after using the module for group treatment in this quasi-experimental study, whereas the conventional method for group control. The data analysis results indicate that action learning and facilitation (L&F), which is supported by the iHOTS module, can already raise students' dominance in mathematics across the board for all four HOTS levels. The research's conclusions indicate a substantial difference between the group control and the group treatment when it comes to the growth of the students' HOTS in mathematics while using the iHOTS technique for level apply, analyze, evaluate, create, as well as whole. To sum up, research like this can help everyone-the Malaysian Ministry of Education (MoE), the school administration, parents, mathematics teachers, and even students-by providing evidence of its efficacy in empowering HOTS mathematics in Malaysia through the enactment of relevant policies and applications.

articleTitle: Gaps Between Expectations and Facts Towards STEM E-Learning in Electrical and Electronics Sciences during the COVID-19 Pandemic in RAVTE University Network
abstract: This research aims to explore expectations and facts in online learning management for the Electrical and Electronics Sciences discipline. The study focuses on three key aspects: competencies in electrical and electronics, e-learning preparation, and learning satisfaction. The sample group in this research was undergraduate students majoring in Electrical and Electronics Sciences or related fields from Ho Chi Minh City University of Technology and Education (HCMUTE), Rajamangala University of Technology Thanyaburi (RMUTT), and Universitas Pendidikan Indonesia (UPI). These students, who registered for the academic year 2023, engaged in partially or entirely online learning during the COVID-19 pandemic. The sample group of 200 individuals was selected using a multi-stage random sampling method. The research results indicate that the mean of gaps between expectations and facts in e-learning management for Electrical and Electronics Sciences, along with their standard deviations (1.37, 0.97), can be categorized into competencies of Electrical and Electronics Sciences, e-learning preparations, and satisfaction. The gaps in all 10 indicators related to e-learning management in Electrical and Electronics Sciences 11.283)) were found to be significantly different at the 0.05 significance level.

articleTitle: Research on Key Elements of Total Quality Management of Online Teaching in Colleges and Universities: Based on Grounded Theory
abstract: This research explores the fundamental components of Total Quality Management (TQM) in online teaching at colleges and universities through the lens of grounded theory. The study highlights the pivotal role of teaching and education in higher education institutions and emphasizes the direct influence of teaching quality on student development. With the increasing adoption of online teaching methodologies such as blended learning and flipped classrooms, the advantages and potential of online education have become increasingly apparent. The research investigates the correlation between quality issues and quality control within the framework of TQM, emphasizing its application in higher education to enhance teaching quality. The study utilizes grounded theory to analyze and synthesize data from CNKI literature, policy documents in China, and interviews with educators, leading to the identification of 34 concepts that contribute to enhancing online teaching quality. These concepts are classified into 12 domains and 6 main categories, which are integrated into a theoretical model for TQM in online teaching. The research concludes that a systematic approach to TQM is crucial for continuously improving online teaching quality while aligning with students' educational needs as well as societal demands.

articleTitle: Implementation Model of Capstone Project Through Collaborative Project-Based Learning Using Application of Project Management
abstract: Capstone Project (CP) is a project-based learning method (PbL) that enables students to utilize the information acquired in college to solve real-world problems. There are still deficiencies in implementing CP within the Outcomes-Based Education (OBE) curriculum. According to OBE curricular standards, process improvements are necessary to achieve precise and measurable learning outcomes. The OBE curriculum focuses on learning outcomes and the difficulties of establishing achievement standards and accurate evaluation. This study examines the CP implementation paradigm using the project management application (PMA). Implementing CP online presents challenges such as coordination, time management, and tracking of project progress. This study uses a quantitative research design with a survey approach to investigate PMA's efficacy in implementing CP. The research involved 156 participants chosen using purposive sampling methods. The research questionnaire assesses student motivations, participation, and partnerships. Data analysis shows that PMA positively affects student motivation, engagement, and cooperation, strengthening the CP process. The results offer significant information for making informed judgments and improving educational practices to improve student learning outcomes and overall academic quality.

articleTitle: Game-Based Rapid Analysis and Discuss (G-BRAND) Learning Model: A Unique and Fun Learning Experience to Public Sector Accounting Courses)
abstract: This study aims to produce the concept of a game-based rapid analysis and discuss model of learning in public sector accounting courses and the impact on learning after using this learning innovation. The background of this research is the saturation and level of understanding of students in public sector accounting courses that are not optimal due to conventional learning models. The research method used is Research and Development. The data were analyzed through the normalized gain score measure to measure the improvement of process skills and cognitive learning outcomes between before and after learning. The results of this study indicate that the combination of games, videos, and discussions in learning media can provide a unique and fun learning experience so that both lecturers and students have the opportunity to absorb knowledge more easily and optimally. It is hoped that this research can provide information and options for using a more modern and effective learning model to increase student critical analysis

articleTitle: Enhancing Industry's Role in Vocational Education: An Analysis of Challenges and Opportunities Based on a Literature Review
abstract: Enhancing industry engagement in vocational education is a crucial strategy for refining the quality of graduates to meet the continuously evolving job market needs. This article conducts a systematic review of the existing literature to identify the challenges and opportunities in industry involvement in vocational education. Through in-depth analysis of various sources, the article reveals that the skill gap between the vocational education curriculum and industry needs remains a significant issue. This challenge is exacerbated by assessment and certification systems that often do not accurately reflect the actual competencies required by the industry. Furthermore, the article explores opportunities through internship and work placement programs that enable students to gain relevant experience, as well as strategic partnerships between educational institutions and industries to develop responsive curricula. The article also recommends enhancing the synergy between vocational education and industry through policies that support this integration, which will not only improve the quality of vocational education but also expand employment opportunities for graduates. This research indicates that more integrated and sustained cooperation between vocational education and the industrial sector is key to ensuring the relevance of education with the dynamics of the global job market.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Intention for the Student's Adoption of Artificial Intelligence for Learning Activities in Education-Based University
abstract: Technology is developing to provide new experiences resembling human intelligence, called artificial intelligence (AI). AI technology can be applied in various aspects of science and life, including education. Therefore, a study will explore some factors in student that can encourage the intention to adopt artificial intelligence for learning activities at Universitas Negeri Malang (UM). UM is one of the best universities in the education field in Indonesia. This research aims to examine the factors influencing AI adoption in learning activities in higher education. The study will be developed using the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) model. This study used 251 students from UM. The researchers used SEM-PLS to analyze the data. The findings showed that performance expectancy and perceived risk significantly influenced on attitudes toward AI, which in turn can lead to the adoption of AI in Higher education. AI has a significant impact on learning activities in the classroom. In addition, the AI price does not influence the use of AI by students in higher education.

articleTitle: Digital Business Center as an Optimization of Digital Business Literacy and Entrepreneurship Education
abstract: Technological developments affect the way entrepreneurs operate, so online business is a profitable opportunity. “Lapas Perempuan Malang”/ Correctional Institution has productive human resources to create high-value products. This research method is Research and Development with the ADDIE model. The results of the material validation consisting of aspects of material content, language and communication, and presentation received 86.4%, so it was considered very valid and feasible. The results of media expert validation consisting of aspects of navigation, visuals, and communication received a result of 82.5%, so it is considered valid and feasible to use as a means of entrepreneurship education and promotional media. The results of the comments and suggestions given are that the website-based Digital Business Center media is good. However, explanations of existing features can be clarified to make it easier to understand and use optimally. Based on the trial results, this digital business center is excellent in terms of language and attractiveness. It can increase the desire to learn entrepreneurship and provide entrepreneurial experience for the community. This Digital Business Center media can be a digital marketing platform for products from prisoners.

articleTitle: Transformative Development of Vocational Education Management through Thai-Meister Framework: A Case Study of Kampong Chheuteal Institute of Technology, Kingdom of Cambodia
abstract: This study aimed to enhance vocational education management using the Thai-Meister model at Kampong Chheuteal Institute of Technology (KCIT), Kingdom of Cambodia. The process involved: 1) Developing the vocational education curriculum, 2) Procuring equipment, and machinery, and designing laboratory layouts, 3) Conducting training sessions for KCIT teachers, 4) Creating teaching materials aligned with Thai-Meister guidelines, and 5) Executing the teaching and learning process. The sample comprised 17 undergraduate students specializing in Electrical major at KCIT. Research tools included: 1) Lesson plans for the Electrical System Installation course, 2) Teaching aids and materials such as handouts, job sheets, practical electrical system installation experiments, and PLC programming resources, 3) Theoretical knowledge assessment forms, and 4) Practical skills assessment forms. Findings revealed an 82.35% pass rate among all students in the competency test, with an average score of 65.00% for both theory and practical components.

articleTitle: Enhancing Science Education in Thailand: Implementing the CER Framework to Improve PISA Performance and Student Argumentation
abstract: Recent PISA results indicate a concerning trend in the science competence of Thai students, highlighting the urgent need for educational reform. This paper explores the transformative potential of the Claim-Evidence-Reasoning (CER) approach to address these challenges in Thai science education. It advocates for a shift from traditional contentfocused instruction to a competency-based learning framework that emphasises abilities to explain phenomena scientifically, evaluate and design scientific inquiries, and interpret data and evidence scientifically. Specific transformations proposed include revising educational goals to focus on depth of understanding and practical application, redesigning classroom activities to foster active learning and inquiry through the CER approach and adapting assessment methods to prioritise formative feedback over summative scores. These strategic shifts, aligned with the PISA 2025 framework, aim to enhance student engagement and proficiency in science, thus improving their readiness to meet international standards and succeed in a globally competitive environment.

articleTitle: Enhanced IoT-Based Simulation for Air Handling Unit (AHU) Operational Training
abstract: In the evolving educational technology landscape, integrating Internet of Things (IoT) technologies transforms traditional teaching and learning approaches into more active, collaborative, and self-directed processes. This study introduces an advanced teaching solution to enhance engineering education, particularly in air conditioning and refrigeration: the IoT-embedded Simulation of Teaching Aids for Air Handling Unit (AHU) Operation. Utilising the comprehensive ADDIE instructional design model, this project progressed through five phases: analysis, design, development, implementation, and evaluation. The IoT integration facilitates real-time data monitoring and interactive learning experiences, offering a hands-on approach to understanding complex engineering concepts. Three domain experts rigorously evaluated the effectiveness of this teaching aid through a series of assessments focusing on design, development, and functionality. Feedback from these evaluations confirmed the teaching aid's success in engaging students and enhancing their learning process. Recognised for its quality materials, safety, and organised components, along with its innovative use of IoT technology, this product successfully fulfils the objectives of this study. It represents a significant step forward in modernising engineering education.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence with hands-on exercises: maze-solver, crawling robot and emotion recognition
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is a pivotal technology with diverse applications in fields such as algorithm design, robotic automation, image processing, and machine learning. This paper introduces three accessible examples designed to demystify core AI techniques for educational purposes: navigating mazes with the A* search algorithm, teaching a virtual robot through Q-learning, and recognizing patterns in images using Principal Component Analysis. Accompanied by theoretical discussions, algorithmic breakdowns, and interactive Python simulations, these exercises aim to engage and educate beginners in the basic functionalities and applications of AI

articleTitle: Implementing a Constructionist Project-Based Learning Approach to Enhance Chemistry Learning Achievement in Eleventh Grade Students
abstract: Chemistry plays a vital role in our daily lives. However, student engagement in this subject has been traditionally low, leading to poor academic performance. Project-Based Learning (PBL) has emerged as a promising solution to this issue. Despite this, there has been limited research investigating PBL within a constructionist learning environment. This study aims to implement a constructionist PBL approach to enhance students' learning achievements in chemistry. The study involved 15 eleventh-grade students selected through convenience sampling. A constructionist PBL approach was implemented, and data on students' learning achievements in chemistry were collected using pre- and post-tests. Data were analyzed using a paired t-test. The findings indicate that the constructionist PBL approach significantly improved the students' learning achievement in chemistry (p < 0.05). Moreover, the application of this approach in the study markedly enhanced the learning achievements of the Grade 11 students. This educational approach not only supports the generation of self-knowledge but also fosters the development of critical thinking skills, which are crucial for constructing knowledge.

articleTitle: Platform of RMUT Talent Resource Management for reforming the National Manpower System
abstract: This paper presents an inspiring new platform for human resources development in Thailand, which uses science and technology (S&T) to overcome the Middle-Income Trap. The platform aims to reform the national manpower system and create a highly skilled workforce to meet the demands of the growing industries. By leveraging the expertise of RMUT talents and grooming young talents, the platform promotes cooperation between students, faculty members, and enterprises on R&D projects. In addition, it facilitates the utilization of RMUT's R&D projects at companies through the mentor shadow system. The results show that the RMUT talent resource management platform can be used to reform the national manpower system and strengthen the university-industry linkage. This platform is a testament to the power of innovation and collaboration, and it inspires all those seeking to promote human resource development and economic growth through science and technology.

articleTitle: Integrated Problem-Based Learning with Moodle to Enhance Problem-Solving Skills among Employees
abstract: Training in today's organizations faces rapid changes in a continuously organization and technology environment. Training models used in the past may no longer be able to meet the needs. Moreover, training requires a certain amount of time that may affect working hours. This research focuses on strengthening training programs and developing the problem-solving skills of employees within the organization. The Moodle technology was applied to support the learning environment for problem-based learning. Blended learning, including five steps was used as face-to-face and online learning. The steps include problem-facing, problem exploration, problem-solving actions, evaluation, and conclusion. The findings indicated that integrating problem-based learning with Moodle enhances problem-solving skills among employees. This approach encouraged the employees to identify problems, analyze relevant data relating to the problem, use a solution approach, and summarize problems. Therefore, the ability of finding solutions were developed in the production line. Besides, the findings revealed reducing the burden on the training room and disturbance of the working hours of both the trainer and employees

articleTitle: Development of E-Module of Heutagogy Learning Approach for Measuring Instruments Course, Electrical Technology Certificate Programme in Community College
abstract: Teaching approaches are important in assisting lecturers in efficiently planning and delivering their lectures. Technological advancements should be applied not just for internet access and communication, but also in the teaching and learning (TnL) process. This study was designed to develop a website-based E-Module of the heutagogy learning approach to improve the teaching and learning process in the Measurement Tools Course, Electrical Technology Certificate Program in Community Colleges. The proposed E-Module is expected to make the lectures more engaging and effective for students. A product design and development approach was employed in this study to collect data from 15 respondents, comprising five experts and ten lecturers from the Southern Zone Community College. The usability of the E-Module in terms of interface design, interaction, content, and heutagogy learning approach was assessed through expert evaluation forms and user questionnaires. Resultantly, the usability evaluation of this EModule revealed a high degree of agreement in terms of interface design, interaction, and content. Respondents also agreed that utilizing the heutagogy learning approach is incredibly relevant and may improve lecturers’ teaching sessions. Nevertheless, larger-scale research is needed to assess the efficiency and effectiveness of this E-Module of heutagogy learning approach in enhancing students' knowledge and competencies, particularly in the Measurement Tools Course.

articleTitle: Universal Design for Learning: Storytelling Application to Promote Learning for Children with Deaf
abstract: The objective of this study is to create and implement a storytelling application that enhances the vocabulary acquisition of second-grade kids who are deaf, and to assess the efficacy of the application. Research instruments include pre-test and post-test vocabulary evaluation questionnaires, as well as intra-class vocabulary assessments. The purpose of the application is to enhance reading and vocabulary skills through interactive storytelling, incorporating Thai sign language and educational games. The results revealed the impressive effectiveness of the developed application. The performance value calculated from the pre-class and post-class tests yielded a score of 80 out of 80.5, indicating the successful development of the application. This method is highly efficient and appropriate for implementation in the education of Grade 2 students who have hearing difficulties.

articleTitle: Digital Technology Integration in TVET for Tourism: A Case Study for an Android-Based Application Development and Implementation
abstract: This research develops an Android-based tourist information and guide service application, aimed at enhancing digital adaptation in Technical Vocational Education and Training (TVET) sector of the tourism industry. Utilizing the Research and Development (R&D) approach, this project adopts the ADDIE (Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, Evaluation) model to systematically develop and evaluate the application. The research involved 330 end-users and 50 tourism management professionals across various tourist destinations in West Java as the primary population and sample. Data were gathered using performance evaluations and user feedback surveys to assess the application's impact on enhancing human resource competencies within the tourism sector. The findings demonstrate that the application significantly improves service quality and operational efficiency, fosters digital fluency among tourism professionals, and enhances employment opportunities through better resource management and visitor engagement. This underscores the critical role of integrating IT, Big Data, and artificial intelligence in revolutionizing tourism services.

articleTitle: Fostering Synergies: A Dynamic Approach to Collaborative Teaching and Learning in Vocational Education for Industrial Robotics Technology between Changzhou Vocational Institute of Mechatronics Technology and Rajamangala University of Technology Thanyaburi
abstract: This study aimed to design a collaborative teaching and learning approach in Industrial Robotics Technology between Changzhou Vocational Institute of Mechatronics Technology (CZIMT) and Rajamangala University of Technology Thanyaburi (RMUTT). The process included: (1) Development of joint training programs, comprising two courses: Vocational Training Program in Industrial Robotics Technology (Short-Term) and Expert Training Program in Industrial Robotics Technology (Long-Term); (2) Preparation of teaching aids, equipment, and training materials; (3) Implementation of block-course training; (4) Evaluation of professional competencies in both theoretical and practical aspects; and (5) Credit/unit competency transfer within the curriculum. The sample group consisted of second-year students pursuing a Bachelor of Science in Technical Education, specializing in Electronics and Automation Systems Engineering at the Faculty of Technical Education, RMUTT. The group, comprising six students, was selected using a specific sampling method. The results indicated that all students passed the professional competency assessment, with an overall average of 92.67% in both theoretical knowledge and practical skills. The joint curriculum design and collaborative teaching involve RMUTT offering foundational courses in the first year. In the second year, students enroll in short-term block courses at CZIMT, training according to jointly determined competencies. This approach equips students with knowledge and skills that align with RMUTT's curriculum and allows for course credit transfer.

articleTitle: Enhancing Student Comprehension in Aviation Science and Aircraft Construction through Hands-On and Experiential Learning
abstract: While numerous research studies have demonstrated that students effectively acquire learning knowledge through hands-on learning activities, there remains a shortage of studies specifically focusing on the effectiveness of aviation-themed activities in K-12 education. This study aims to develop and implement an aviation-themed intervention that integrates hands-on and experimental learning methods to enhance students’ comprehension of aviation science and aircraft construction. The participants comprised 33 students from various grades at Royal High School Na Yao in Chachoengsao province, selected through purposeful sampling techniques. The experiment lasted for 3 days, with data collected before and after the experiment using a test assessing learning achievement in aviation science and aircraft construction. The results of paired simple t-tests indicated a significant difference between pre- and posttest scores, with the mean score of the posttest being higher than that of the pretest, demonstrating an improvement in students’ comprehension. This study offers empirical evidence supporting the effectiveness of hands-on aviation education interventions in K-12 settings.

articleTitle: The Impact of Digital Role-Playing Games in Engineering Education: A Preliminary Review
abstract: Integrating Digital Role-Playing Games (DRPGs) into engineering education (EE) is a response to the evolving demands of the digital era and the need for innovative educational methods. DRPGs, as a subset of digital game-based learning, enhance student engagement, learning motivation, and outcomes by offering immersive, interactive experiences that align with the cognitive and developmental needs of “digital native learners.” Through a preliminary review, this study assesses DRPGs' impact on EE, explores the challenges and processes of implementing these games into curricula, and investigates the theoretical foundations supporting their use. The findings suggest that DRPGs can significantly improve understanding and application of engineering concepts, foster essential skills, and motivate students. However, effective implementation requires addressing pedagogical integration, technological compatibility, and curriculum alignment challenges. The article calls for further research to solidify DRPGs' role in EE and outlines a path for educators and policymakers to harness their potential for preparing future engineers facing complexities of modern technological landscapes.

articleTitle: SPS Teacher's Perception of STEAM Concepts
abstract: The STEAM concept has become an everyday part of early childhood life processes that can be stimulated in a structured manner through early childhood education (ECE) services. One of the non-formal ECE services, namely SPS, provides educational services for children aged zero to six years. This study aimed to determine the perceptions of SPS teachers towards the STEAM concept, considering that SPS teachers do not get professional teacher education as early childhood teachers do in formal education paths. Eighty SPS teachers spread across SPS institutions in Malang, East Java, participated in the survey by filling out a questionnaire distributed via Google Forms. STEAM concepts in this research, including perceived knowledge, classroom settings, and practices, were described in the questionnaires distributed. The analysis results showed no influence of age, years of experience, educational background, or participation in professional training on the perception of STEAM concepts of SPS teachers. Participating in professional training activities strengthens SPS teachers' confidence in the STEAM concept applied in their classrooms. SPS teachers still need professional training organized by the government to improve their perceptions of the STEAM concept, where the training they attend independently has provided initial confidence in their perceptions of the importance of the STEAM concept.

articleTitle: Enhancing STEM Project Instructional Competence: A Short Training Camp for Secondary School Teachers in Thailand
abstract: STEM education is essential, yet the lack of STEM teachers is prevalent in many educational sectors, including Thailand. This study investigated the effects of a short-term training camp focusing on STEM projects on secondary STEM teachers' instructional competence. The main training activities in this program are workshops about the STEM process and hands-on activities where participants practice being mentors for students' STEM projects. On the first and the last day of the program, participants were assessed using the multiple-choice questions for the content knowledge and the self-evaluation form with Likert-scale questions for the skills and attitudes. Eight participants with the most and least improvement test scores were invited to join a semi-structured interview. The quantitative data from 29 participants were analyzed using descriptive statistics and the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. The results show that all aspects of participants' instructional competence significantly improved after the program. The data from the interviews also support the findings and reveal that workshops and hands-on activities are the keys to their improvement.

articleTitle: Improving Students' Attitudes toward STEM and Their Interest in STEM Careers: A Collaborative Learning Approach
abstract: Today, the main driver of the economy is innovation, much of which comes from advances in science, technology, mathematics and engineering (STEM). Developing high-quality human resources in the STEM field is a breakthrough in implementing socio-economic strategies in each country and STEM education plays a key role. In addition, for STEM education to be effective, improving students' attitudes toward STEM and interest in STEM careers is very important. We conducted this study to examine whether and how collaborative learning environments impact changes in students' attitudes toward STEM as well as their level of interest in STEM careers. By organizing a controlled experimental study for 81 middle school students (84 control groups), in which both groups participated in a 4-week STEM course with the same course content but the experimental group was taught using a collaborative learning method. Research results show that the collaborative learning environment promoted students' attitudes toward STEM in the experimental group higher than in the control group (the increase for each content ranged from 0.23 - 0.36 scores), and their level of interest in STEM careers in the experimental group is also 0.28 scores higher than the control group, the above differences are statistically significant. This result is important evidence for teachers and educational institutions to have more options in using active educational methods to meet the goals of STEM education.

articleTitle: Development of an Engineering Drawing Course Structure with CAD Software Integration using Multi-Level Rubric Assessment
abstract: As 3-D CAD modeling has become preferred drawing and drafting methods, most engineering organizations and educational institutions have to include the teaching of 3-D CAD modeling into their program. However, the integration of CAD into traditional drawing course was proved to be a difficult task due to an enormous design space and high level of interactions. This paper aimed to design a systematic procedure based on a multi-level rubric approach for integrating 3-D CAD modeling into an engineering drawing course. Firstly, the course learning outcomes was defined to guide as main objectives. The required CAD skills for achieving these CLOs were then defined. The mapping of tasks assigned with a specific set of skills was carefully performed. By combining the required skills matrix and the mapping between tasks and skills, the multi-level rubric was then formed. The rubric was used to evaluate the CAD learning quality. Its observations and discussions were then analyzed and proved to be useful. Thus, the proposed procedure can be used to help design the course structure of related topics in the near future.
